rows.name: Ann Marie Guenther Memorial Scholarship
values: The Ann Marie Guenther Memorial Scholarship is provided by her loving husband Mark. Mark recognizes that education has the possibility to opens doors and create brighter futures. He intends to carry forth this outlook and also honor the passion Ann had for living life to the fullest through this memorial scholarship. The scholarship is open to high school seniors enrolled at Whitefish High School or Whitefish Independent High School who aspire to pursue higher education in a 2-year ($5K available) or 4-year (up to $10K available) college or university (12 credit minimum per semester). Paper applications to Mrs. Jones by 4/10.

rows.name: The LeRoy W. Homer Jr. Foundation Scholarship
values: The LeRoy W. Homer Jr. Foundation, P.O. Box 268, Marlton, NJ 08053
The LeRoy W. Homer Jr. Foundation Scholarship

The LeRoy W. Homer Jr. Foundation empowers future aviators to pursue their dreams of flight, honoring LeRoy’s legacy. The foundation builds a community of pilots embodying values of leadership, excellence, and service.

rows.name: Montana Premier Scholarship
values: This is an automatic, merit-based scholarship for Montana freshmen demonstrating academic promise based on their cumulative high school GPA. Award amounts vary based on GPA, ranging from $1,000 to $4,000 per year, and are renewable for four years for tuition only. Students are automatically considered upon submitting an application for admission with a self-reported GPA.

rows.name: UM Academic Achievement Scholarship
values: This scholarship is automatically considered for new students pursuing their first bachelor's degree when they apply for admission to the University of Montana.

rows.name: Pell Promise for Montana Students
values: The Pell Promise for Montana Students is a financial aid initiative by Carroll College for Montana residents who are Federal Pell Grant recipients. It provides significant financial assistance, covering tuition, to eligible students who maintain a 3.0 GPA, reside on-campus, and accept a federal Stafford loan. It aims to enhance accessibility and affordability for under-served Montanans pursuing a Catholic, liberal arts education.

rows.name: Blue Collar Brain Scholarship Program
values: This scholarship awards $2,500 to a student pursuing an education in any skilled trade. Applicants must be US citizens or have a student visa, be a high school graduate or GED recipient, and be enrolled or plan to enroll full-time in a vocational/technical school or 2-year college for the fall 2025 semester, planning to acquire certification or degree in a skilled trade program. A GPA of 3.0 or higher is required.

rows.name: Don K Chevrolet- Subaru- Chrysler – Dodge – Jeep - Ram Scholarship
values: Don K Chevrolet- Subaru- Chrysler – Dodge – Jeep - Ram Scholarship

$1000 Scholarship will be awarded to one qualifying student from each of the following High Schools: Whitefish, Eureka, Bigfork, Columbia Falls, Glacier High and Flathead High, School Graduate; financial need and extracurricular/ community involvement in addition to higher-education plans are assessed; Application to be mailed to: Don K Whitefish, PO BOX 1178, Whitefish, MT 59937

rows.name: Alcohol Responsibility Matters Scholarship
values: CARD will award five, one-time, $2,000 scholarships for Montana seniors graduating high school in 2026 who come up with a design and write a brief paragraph (250 words maximum explaining the design) to create posters, T-shirts, stickers or decals, coasters, etc., dedicated to the question: What does “Alcohol Responsibility Matters” mean to you and your community? To qualify, high school seniors must be in good academic standing with their current institution of learning. If chosen, the funds will then be deposited with their school/apprentice program/certificate institute of higher learning. Applications (online or mailed) must be received by midnight Jan 25th 2026.

rows.name: Glacier Bank Scholarship
values: Include transcript, senior resume and answer 2 brief essays: 1) Please explain your financial needs 2) Brief statement on education and career goals. Submit to Mrs. Jones by end of day 4/15.

rows.name: Black Mountain Software Scholarship (2 - $1,000)
values: Black Mountain Software will be awarding two $1,000.00 scholarships to graduating seniors in Montana. Any Montana high school senior graduating in 2026 may apply if he or she will be attending an accredited institution of higher education. These accredited institutions include trade schools, technical schools, colleges or universities. The applicant’s field of study may be any field that they want to pursue. Applications and essays must be submitted electronically to Black Mountain Software. Please see the scholarship application for instructions for completing the application form and requirements for the essay. All submissions must be received before midnight on or before February 26th, 2026. Essay Question: If you were given a team of developers to build one new piece of software (an app, a program, a game) that would make the world a more joyful, curious, or connected place, what would it be and why? Describe its core function and the problem it solves for its users. The essay is limited to 2000 characters (300-350 words) or less.

rows.name: Hawkins Scholarship
values: Checklist to be completed and submitted

rows.name: Clearwater Credit Union Scholarship (8 - $2,500)
values:
• Be a Clearwater Credit Union member for at least six months.
• Be a 2026 graduating high school senior OR a post-high school adult learner entering or enrolled in college.
• Have at least one transaction on any Clearwater deposit account within the last 60 days.
• Complete an online Financial Wellness Checkup in Clearwater’s online Financial Education Center by March 31, 2026, at 11:59pm.
• Check-up results are for informational purposes only and do NOT factor into scholarship consideration.
• Complete an online scholarship application by March 31, 2026, at 11:59pm.

rows.name: The Luedke Family Scholarship
values: A student can apply; in addition a member of the Whitefish community can nominate them. This scholarship is available to graduating seniors of Whitefish High School or Whitefish Independent High School who have experienced hardships, challenges due to disability, or discrimination in some way including but not limited to: economically (low-income), marginalized racially/ethnically, etc.  Paper applications to Mrs. Jones by 4/4.

rows.name: John Michaels Memorial Scholarship ($2,000)
values: Eligibility: Open to high school seniors enrolled at Whitefish High School who aspire to pursue further education in a 4-year, 2-year, or technical school within Montana. • Application Requirements: Interested students must submit the application form along with an essay addressing the provided prompt. Essays should be kept under 500 words. • No Minimum GPA Requirement: We believe in the potential of every student and encourage all eligible candidates to apply. Submit to Mrs. Jones by end of 4/11.

rows.name: Herriges Family Memorial Scholarship (3) $3000
values: The Herriges Family Memorial Scholarship was established in memory of Nicholas and Anastasia Herriges by their children, all of whom were educated in the Whitefish schools. Grades, employment, extracurricular activities, community service and financial need are considered. Return applications to Mrs. Jones by: 4/20/26.

rows.name: Horatio Alger Association - Career & Technical Candidates
values: Horatio Alger Association - Career & Technical Candidates

While most other scholarships focus exclusively on academic achievement or leadership potential, Horatio Alger Scholarships are also intended for promising students who have critical financial need ($100,000 or lower adjusted gross family income is required), demonstrate integrity and perseverance in overcoming adversity, and are determined to succeed. NOTE: By filling out one application, you will be considered for all scholarships for which you are eligible (but you will need to know WHICH scholarships you are interested in and select them from a list within your application)

rows.name: Ortho Rehab "Reach Your Peak"
values: Please attach a short, typed, essay (500 word maximum), explaining how this scholarship will help you “Reach Your Peak”.  You can return the completed applications to  Ms. Jones, your High School Career Guidance Counselor no later than April 1, 2026.

rows.name: Whitefish Lake Institute Ripple Effect Scholarship
values: Whitefish Lake Institute Ripple Effect Scholarship

This scholarship is available to any Whitefish High School senior who is entering a four year university with plans to major in an environmental science field. Eligible majors include; environmental science/studies, environmental engineering, biology, and sustainability. Other majors will be considered if they demonstrate a link to an environmental emphasis. A brief essay also needs to be included (300-500 words) describing your “watershed ethic.” In short, what is your philosophy regarding human activities that affect water quality in the Whitefish Lake Watershed? How does your watershed ethic make you a good steward of water resources in the Whitefish Lake Watershed? Paper applications to be mailed to: Whitefish Lake Institute, Ripple Effect Applications 550 E. 1st St. #103 Whitefish, MT 59937 or emailed to: Info@whitefishlake.org // Subject: Ripple Effect Application

rows.name: VFW Voices of Democracy - Patriotic Audio Essay “How Are You Showing Patriotism And Support For Our Country?”
values: VFW Veterans of Foreign Wars Information
VFW Voices of Democracy - Patriotic Audio Essay “How Are You Showing Patriotism And Support For Our Country?”

All entries must start with the local VFW post. Contact the Whitefish VFW to see about participating. Record your original 3-5 minute (+ or – 5 second max.) audio essay on a flash drive, or other electronic device. Hearing/speech impaired students should email the Voice of Democracy National Office at youth scholarships@vfw.org for special instructions. No music, singing, poetry or sound effects are allowed. The body of the essay must not identify you in any way, (including, but not limited to your name, school, city, state, race, or national origin) although the recording & typed essay should be labeled with your name, to show ownership. All entries competing at the local Post level must be in the hands of that VFW Post by midnight, Oct. 31, 2025.  Originality is worth 35 points (treatment of the theme should show imagination and human interest), Content is worth 30 points (clearly express your ideas in an organized manner. Fully develop your theme and use transitions to move smoothly from one idea to another), Delivery is worth 35 points (speak in a clear and credible manner). Read application for further details. You will submit the recording, typed essay and this completed entry form to: Dustin Wegner, Commander     20 Baker Ave., Whitefish, MT  59937 (you can mail or drop off in person). Call Dustin Wegner with questions: 406.654.4020

rows.name: Elks Most Valuable Student Scholarship
values: You do NOT need to be related to the Elks organization to apply! Students judged on scholarship and leadership. They are interested in students who are passionate about making a positive IMPACT on society. You do not have to be a member (or the dependent of a member) of the Elks. You will fill out online brief information about academic and leadership experience, in addition to providing a resume and counselor recommendation form. You will also answer the following essay question: Using one of the leadership roles or extracurricular activities you prioritized as being important to you, describe what impact the experience had on you, what you contributed, what you learned about yourself, and how it has influenced your plans for the future. (500 word max). WHen completing your online application, list KALISPELL POST code for sponsoring chapter (this has been confirmed with the State Scholarship Chair). Per State Scholarship Chair, VOLUNTEERISM is key to highlight. Questions? Contact: Dan Riddle 406-204-3054 dannyriddle406@yahoo.com

rows.name: Jack Kent Cooke Scholarship Program
values: Senior, 3.75 GPA, Family gross income of less than $95,000. The application is online and via using the Common App. You will complete the Common App general requirements, which include things like your contact information, the school you attend and your grades, and your activities and honors. You will also invite your school counselor and two teachers to submit recommendations through the Common App. Once you have created a Common App, add the Jack Kent Cooke Foundation as one of your “schools” to access the application questions that are specific to the College Scholarship Program. These will include: Eligibility, Several short essays, Extracurricular activities and honors, Intended major, Financial information, including the last three years’ Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) for your household. Candidates are reviewed and selected based on leadership, academic ability and achievement, persistence, and unmet financial need.

rows.name: MT DOT Aviation Scholarships
values: These scholarships are offered to help defray costs of education (e.g., flight instruction, aircraft airframe and powerplant (A&P) mechanic school, etc.). Recipients will be announced in January 2026. Note special instructions for HOW to submit your application (they are very specific and will determine whether your application is viewed as "complete" by the organization)!

rows.name: National Honor Society Member Scholarship
values: This year, we are awarding $2 million in scholarships to 600 students. Each year, scholarship recipients are selected based on their demonstration of the four pillars of NHS: Scholarship, Service, Leadership, and Character. Senior in NHS, NHS student account holder, attending an accredited college/university in the U.S. In the application process you will need to provide detailed information about activities and experiences related to scholarship, service, leadership, and character. You will also need to request an Adviser Certification from your NHS Adviser (acts as a short recommendation form and confirms the applicant is currently in good standing with a local NHS chapter. Request a Recommendation from one non-adviser, non-family member adult who can speak to the applicant’s commitment to the pillars of NHS. The recommendation must be completed in the application portal and no external documents or communications will be accepted.

rows.name: Hagan Scholarship
values: The Hagan Scholarship is a nationwide need-based merit scholarship, designed to provide recipients with the opportunity to graduate college debt-free. Applicants must attend a traditional public high school governed by a school district. Free workshops, Free Schwab Brokerage Accounts and Free Study Abroad provide recipients with a practical understanding of important life skills not typically covered in the school curriculum. (Hagan Scholarship Brochure). Applicant’s Adjusted Gross Household Income reported for 2023 Federal Income Tax Purposes must not have exceeded $100,000. “Household Income” is defined as the total income received by all members of a household living under the same roof. Applicants must show evidence they will be working 240 hours from January 1, 2026 to September 1, 2026 (they understand that most recipients work during the summer months. Work can be part-time during their senior year in high school or full-time during the summer or a combination of the two. They are looking for "students willing to contribute toward their educational expenses."

rows.name: Montana Jaycee Foundation Scholarship
values: Each year, the U.S. Junior Chamber International (JCI) Senate Foundation grants $1,500 scholarships to graduating high school seniors who plan to continue their education at accredited post-secondary colleges and universities. NOTE: there is a different application form for those applying to an Undergraduate vs. Vocational school! Application for Either postmarked BEFORE the 17th to: Janet Prescott 1060 Weaver Road Belgrade, MT 59714 Need to submit *UP TO* 500 word personal statement in addition for *UP TO* 3 letters of recommendation. See application for additional materials. Contact Nancy Salopek via email at scholarship@usjcisenate.org with questions!

rows.name: Montana Jaycee Foundation Scholarship
values: Each year, the U.S. Junior Chamber International (JCI) Senate Foundation grants $1,000 scholarships to graduating high school seniors who plan to continue their education at accredited trade or vocational institution. NOTE: there is a different application form for those applying to an Undergraduate vs. Vocational school! Application for Either postmarked BEFORE the 17th to: Janet Prescott 1060 Weaver Road Belgrade, MT 59714 Need to submit *UP TO* 500 word personal statement in addition for *UP TO* 3 letters of recommendation. See application for additional materials. Contact Nancy Salopek via email at scholarship@usjcisenate.org with questions!

rows.name: Elks National Foundation Legacy Awards
values: For the 2026 contest, any child or grandchild (or step-child, step-grandchild, or legal ward) of a living Elk who joined the Order on or before April 1, 2023, or a charter member of a Lodge that was instituted on or after April 1, 2023, is eligible to apply. The Elk must have paid Lodge dues for the last two contiguous years through March 31, 2026. Great-grandchildren are not eligible.

rows.name: Horatio Alger Association - Dennis R. Washington Montana Scholarship ($10,000 + $5,000 University match = $15,000)
values: Horatio Alger Association - Dennis R. Washington Montana Scholarship ($10,000 + $5,000 University match = $15,000)

A need-based award of up to $15,000 (over four years) for Montana high-school seniors planning a bachelor's degree at a Montana University System school. Requires U.S. citizenship, critical financial need, perseverance through adversity, and activity involvement; recipients maintain a 2.0 GPA. Apply by February 15 (applications open December 1).

rows.name: Horatio Alger Association - Bachelor's Degree Candidates
values: Horatio Alger Association - Bachelor's Degree Candidates
Applicants must meet the following requirements:

rows.name: Flathead Conservation District Scholarship
values: The Flathead Conservation District’s Scholarship is for local high school seniors intending to pursue a degree in natural resources or a related field. A scholarship of $500 will be offered to each local high school in Flathead County and home school students, if applicable. The Flathead Conservation District’s Scholarship is for local high school seniors intending to pursue a degree in natural resources or a related field.  Appropriate courses of study include (but are not limited to) agriculture, animal/range science, forestry, environmental science/engineering, hydrology, land resources, plant science, wildlife biology, etc. The application deadline is  Friday, March 13th
Natural Resources, or a related field

rows.name: Dorothy and Luther Campbell Scholarship ($2,500)
values: Luther Campbell Scholarship - Whitefish Community Foundation

The Campbells created the fund in 2022 as a way to give back to the community they cherish. Applicant must be a graduating senior in Flathead County or Lincoln County, Montana or have graduated from a high school in Flathead County or Lincoln County, Montana within three years of application date.  Preference will be given to individuals with a proven history of community involvement/volunteerism and a strong work ethic. Requires two current letters of reference, written in the calendar year of the application. Reference letters are uploaded by the reference provider, not the applicant. For assistance, contact Jill Seigmund at (406) 863-1781 or jill@whitefishcommunityfoundation.org.

rows.name: Jean Atkinson Driggers Scholarship ($2,500)
values: Jean Atkinson Driggers Scholarship - Whitefish Community Foundation

The scholarship was created in memory of Jean Atkinson Driggers, who taught at Olney-Bissell for 25 years and was passionate about helping children achieve their highest potential. Applicant must have attended Olney Bissell School. Applicant must be a graduating senior in Flathead County, Montana, or have previously graduated from a high school in Flathead County, Montana. Preference will be given to individuals with a proven history of community involvement/volunteerism, and a strong work ethic. Requires two current letters of reference, written in the calendar year of the application. Reference letters are uploaded by the reference provider, not the applicant. For assistance, contact Jill Seigmund at (406) 863-1781 or jill@whitefishcommunityfoundation.org.

rows.name: Montana Coffee Traders Scholarship (2 - $1,000)
values: Montana Coffee Traders Scholarship - Whitefish Community Foundation

(1) - $1000 scholarship will be awarded to an eligible Montana Coffee Traders employee, or to a child or legal dependent of a current employee; (1) - $1000 scholarship will be awarded to an eligible Flathead Valley resident. Preference will be given to individuals with a proven history of community involvement/volunteerism, and a strong work ethic. Requires two current letters of reference, written in the calendar year of the application. Two essays written by the applicant addressing the following topics: 1) Special attribute(s) or accomplishment(s) that set the applicant apart from the crowd and 2) What the applicant believes they are capable of achieving once they have earned a college degree. This may be explained in terms of life goals, career goals, and/or goals within the community Reference letters are uploaded by the reference provider, not the applicant. For assistance, contact Jill Seigmund at (406) 863-1781 or jill@whitefishcommunityfoundation.org.

rows.name: Glacier Restaurant Groups R.I.S.E. Scholarship (2 - $2,500)
values: Glacier Restaurant Group RISE Scholarship Overview - Whitefish Community Foundation

Applicant must be an eligible employee or dependent of an employee (within the past year); preference will be given to individuals with a proven history of community involvement/volunteerism. Part-Time students are also encouraged to apply. Requires two current letters of reference, written in the calendar year of the application. Reference letters are uploaded by the reference provider, not the applicant. -For assistance, contact Jill Seigmund at (406) 863-1781 or jill@whitefishcommunityfoundation.org.

rows.name: Glacier Restaurant Groups R.I.S.E. Scholarship (3 - $1,000)
values: Glacier Restaurant Group RISE Scholarship Overview - Whitefish Community Foundation
Contact the university or college of interest for application information and reference "Glacier Restaurant Group"

(3) scholarships of $1,000 each will be awarded to students enrolled in one of following programs (one scholarship per program): Montana State University, Gallatin College Culinary Arts Program , University of Montana, Big Sky Culinary Institute, Flathead Valley Community College, Culinary Institute of Montana. To apply for one of the $1,000 culinary arts scholarships, contact the university or college of interest for application information.

rows.name: KIITA Foundation ($10,000 - Renewable for up to 4 Years!)
values: KIITA Foundation ($10,000 - Renewable for up to 4 Years!)

JUST FOR WHITEFISH STUDENTS!!! The Kiita Foundation Scholarship (Kiita rhymes with cheetah) was established in 2023 by Jim and Jo-Ann Armstrong. They want to help a high achieving, financially independent student achieve a bachelor's degree. By financially independent, we mean someone who cannot rely on their family to help pay for college.  This award is very generous... up to $10,000 per year and renewable for up to 4 years. The recipient also has the opportunity to participate in all-expense paid service learning trips to Mexico with a cohort of other students.  They are looking for someone who is highly engaged in school and community activities. Again, they need to be financially independent when it comes to paying for college.  
The following essay questions: 1) This scholarship is for students who cannot rely on their family to help pay for college. Please explain why you need the assistance of this scholarship. 2) Please describe any obstacles in your path to high school graduation and how you have overcome them. 3) Please describe why you are interested in pursuing a bachelor’s degree and what you believe you are capable of achieving once you have earned your degree. You may explain this in terms of your life goals, career goals, and/or goals within your community. 4) Describe volunteer activities in which you have chosen to participate, why you chose those particular volunteer activities, and how those experiences have affected your life. Please contact Jill Seigmund at Whitefish Community Foundation with questions: (406) 863-1781 or jill@whitefishcommunityfoundation.org

rows.name: Whitefish Rotary Scholarship ($1,000)
values: The Whitefish Rotary Club will award scholarships to graduating seniors from Whitefish High School. The number and dollar amount of scholarships awarded will depend on the number of quality applications received and approved but will be a minimum of $1000 per scholarship. Scholarships from Whitefish Rotary Club may be used for any higher education pursuit: 2yr programs, 4yr programs, trade and vocational schools. Paper applications to be turned into Mrs. Jones by 3:30 pm on 4/17

rows.name: Whitefish Bulldog Booster Club Scholarships
values: Scholarships are offered to the most qualified students who have participated in listed extracurricular activities while enrolled at WHS. Leadership and community service are also important factors for consideration. Return application to Mrs. Jones by 4/17.

rows.name: EA Hinderman
values: Incomplete applications will NOT be considered. Must be used same year as High School Graduation. Return paper application to Mrs. Jones by: 4/18/25

rows.name: Beta Sigma Phi ($1,000)
values: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO BE FEMALE TO BE AWARDED THE SCHOLARSHIP. You must be a WHS Senior. An international women's organization with local chapters, we are a cultural, social and civic sorority. We provide a scholarship to a deserving graduating high school senior. Return paper applications to Mrs. Jones by: 4/22/24.

rows.name: Big Sky State Games Scholarship ($500)
values: The Big Sky State Games has teamed up with the CHARACTER COUNTS! Coalition and Mountain Alarm Fire and Security to recognize the importance of sportsmanship and character in Montana student athletes. CHARACTER COUNTS! is a nonprofit organization striving to improve the character of today’s youth. It is based on common ethical values that transcend political, religious, socio-economic, and cultural differences. Called the “Six Pillars of Character,” these values are: trustworthiness, respect, responsibility, fairness, caring and citizenship. Character Counts! Scholarship is sponsored by Mountain Alarm Fire and Security. Over the past twenty-four years, the Big Sky State Games has awarded the Character Counts! Scholarship to outstanding Montana female and male student-citizen-athletes involved in the Big Sky State Games. The scholarship can be used for any secondary education after high school. This includes trade schools and community colleges. Only high school juniors during the 2025-2026 school year are eligible for this scholarship. This is to ensure that fellow students can observe the scholarship winners during their senior year and to recognize the traits the students show. You can fill out the application below. It will also be available at all Montana High Schools Guidance Counselor offices.

rows.name: Flathead Electric Coop. Early Childhood Education Scholarship @ FVCC
values: Flathead Electric Coop. Early Childhood Education Scholarship @ FVCC

The Flathead Electric Coop. Early Childhood Education Scholarship supports students enrolled in FVCC’s early childhood education program. You will be automatically considered based on your completed General Application. To complete the General Application, please sign in.

rows.name: FVCC Institutional Scholarships (Over 850 scholarships)
values: FVCC Scholarships Page and Database of Matches

One institutional application automatically considers you for all of Flathead Valley Community College's donor-funded scholarships (hundreds awarded each year). Open to students admitted to FVCC as degree-seeking; complete the FAFSA to be considered for need-based awards. A strong, nearby option for Whitefish seniors. Summer 2026 deadline: April 30, 2026.

rows.name: Montana Tech’s Pre-Apprentice Line Program.
values: Flathead Electric Cooperative offers two $5,000 scholarships a year for students entering Montana Tech's one-semester Pre-Apprentice Line Program (Highlands College, Butte), which trains entry-level lineworkers. Your hometown must be in the co-op's service territory (which includes Whitefish), and you submit an essay on your background, goals, and financial need.

rows.name: Park Side Credit Union Annual Scholarship (Multiple $1000)
values: Park Side Credit Union Annual Scholarship (Multiple $1000)

Park Side Credit Union (headquartered in Whitefish, MT) awards several $1,000 scholarships each year to graduating high-school seniors within its field of membership — eleven western Montana counties including Flathead. A strong local option for Whitefish seniors.

rows.name: Oratory Scholarship
values: 3/8/25 <--- (Date Change as of 3/3 from the C Falls post!)
The applicant or their parent/legal guardian must be a member of Flathead Electric Cooperative and served by the Co-op at their primary residence.

rows.name: Montana Clerk & Recorder's Scholarship (2) $1,000
values: The Montana Association of Clerk and Recorders is offering two $1,000 scholarships to graduating Montana high school seniors attending an in-state post-secondary school. The association is requesting information related to an applicant’s career  objectives, future goals, and any unusual family or personal circumstances that  have influenced their lives. Credits received for work experience as well as  school and community activities should be included in the application.

rows.name: Montana University System Honor Scholarship (Tuition)
values: Scholarship money must be used to attend an accredited post-secondary education institution in Montana

rows.name: The Montana State Golf Association
values: A one-time (non-renewable) scholarship for Montana residents entering their first year of college who hold an active MSGA membership with a GHIN handicap (junior membership is free for ages 18 and under). Requires a school-certified transcript and two appraisal forms; deadline around March 15.

rows.name: The Barbara Mansfield Champion Scholar Award (The Last Best Ride)
values: Barbara Mansfield Champion Scholar Award | TLBR
The Barbara Mansfield Champion Scholar Award (The Last Best Ride)

The Barbara Mansfield Champion Scholar Award is designated for financially qualified women from towns in the Flathead Valley pursuing post-secondary education. A minimum of two, $2,500 scholarships are awarded each year. We strongly encourage women who identify as Black, Indigenous or as a woman of color to apply for this scholarship. Scholar award funds are disbursed directly to the educational institution the scholar plans to attend and are intended to help cover costs of tuition, books, room and board, and instructional supplies.

rows.name: Whitefish Lions Scholarship
values: 2 x $1,000 scholarships available. Due by March 30, 2026. Eligibility: Open to Whitefish High School graduating seniors who are interested in advancing their education by attending a 4-year, 2-year, technical or vocational school. Please submit volunteer service in resume form including dates, location, supervisor contact information, description of volunteer service, etc. Please submit TWO short essays (see application form).

rows.name: Gianforte Trade and Technology Scholarships
values: Gianforte Trade and Tech Scholarship Fact Sheet

A Montana state scholarship of $1,500 per semester (full-time; $750 part-time, renewable up to $6,000) for Montana residents enrolled at least half-time in a qualifying trade or technical program — automotive, plumbing, electrical, construction, diesel, cybersecurity, and more. File the FAFSA and demonstrate unmet financial need. You apply once you are enrolled in the program (fall and spring deadlines).

rows.name: National Farmers Union Scholarships (the "Stanley Moore" and the "Hubert K. and JoAnn Seymour" Scholarships)
values: National Farmers Union Scholarships (the "Stanley Moore" and the "Hubert K. and JoAnn Seymour" Scholarships)
The application deadline is Friday, March 13th.

rows.name: Logan Health - Healthy Futures Scholarship
values: For students who have a passion for health care and are dedicated to making a positive impact on the health and well-being of others. Merit based with 3.0 GPA or higher (preference given for biomedical and college prep courses), service to the school and/or community, essay (300-500 words addressing your higher education plans, short and long-term goals, and why you deserve consideration for this award). Include FAFSA SAR page 1.

rows.name: Ted Lund Scholarship
values: Overview of Ted Lund Memorial Student/Athlete Scholarship

3 TYPED COPIES PAPERCLIPPED TOGETHER of ALL the required materials/paper applications to be submitted to Mrs. Jones by 4/3. YOU MUST HAVE PLAYED ON A WHS TEAM. SHort essay about the impact of sports required. Coach letter of recommendation.

rows.name: Flathead County Farmers Union Scholarship
values: Montana Farmers Union is happy to announce its 2024 scholarships which are made available through special efforts of the MFU Foundation, Montana Farmers Union, Chouteau, Cascade, and Flathead County Farmers Unions. Montana Farmers Union family membership dues must be current. ($50/per family, per year). Scholarships must be used the year they are awarded. Students may receive a scholarship both as a high school senior and once during post-secondary career.

rows.name: MGGA Scholarships
values: For any Montana high school or college student majoring in a degree that will impact rural communities; applications to consider: Scholastic Achievement, School Involvement, Community Involvement, Essay

rows.name: Water and Environmental Technologies Scholarship (2 - $1,000)
values: Diversity Scholarship Application; expand the perspectives shared and voices heard. Preference to underrepresented groups. Essay topic of 300 words: "What is the importance of diversity and inclusion?"  Water & Environmental Technologies, Inc. (WET) is a technical environmental and engineering consulting firm committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace. We believe innovation and creativity come when companies advocate for a varied range of experience, talent, and ideas. To continue our commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion, we are offering a scholarship for first year college students who share our passion and vision to expand the perspectives shared and voices heard. WET will award two (2) $1,000 scholarships. This scholarship is open to Montana and Wyoming High School students, but preference will be given to those who are members of an underrepresented class* (i.e. include, but are not limited to, the following: ethnicity, disability, gender, sexual orientation, income, education, etc.) Paper Application and all required attachments should be submitted to: WATER & ENVIRONMENTAL TECHNOLOGIES   ATTENTION: DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION COMMITTEE   480 EAST PARK STREET    BUTTE, MT 59701  or Applications can also be submitted on our website at the following link:  waterenvtech.com/diversityscholarship

rows.name: Jack Quatman Memorial Scholarship
values: Open to high school seniors enrolled at Whitefish High School who aspire to pursue further education whether it be at a traditional 4-year, 2-year, technical school, or through beginning work/apprenticeship. Interested students must submit a TYPED application form along with an essay addressing the provided prompt. Essays should be kept under 250 words (half page). No Minimum GPA Requirement: We believe in the potential of every student and encourage all eligible candidates to apply. Application to Ms Jones by 4/4

rows.name: Dane Hunt Kindness Scholarship
values: Student can NOT nominate themselves for this scholarship. A member of the Whitefish community must nominate them. Looking for examples of random acts of kindness.

rows.name: John L. and Ann Taylor Scholarship
values: John L. and Ann Taylor Scholarship

FOCUS ON FINE ARTS. Personal essay approximately 300 words/one page. Describe why a college degree in the fine arts is very important to you and include a statement of financial need. Resume, Transcript, Portfolio, and 1 letter of reference are required. Mail (address on form) or email application to rboe@dadco.com by April 10th 2026. If you have any questions, please contact me the Trust Officer, Adrian Snyder at (541) 608-4389 or adsnyder@dadco.com or Renee Boe on rboe@dadco.com

rows.name: Flathead County Democratic Women's Club ($1,500)
values: The purpose of the scholarship is to provide financial assistance to students who are graduates of a Flathead County high school and those currently attending Flathead Valley Community College who wish to pursue higher education or vocational training.  Other criteria are:  a traditional or non-traditional student who already has or is currently completing requirements for a high school diploma or G.E.D.; an individual able to demonstrate financial need; and one who is learning the philosophy of the Democratic Party and continuing their education. The student is asked to include an essay stating the reasons for applying, their educational or vocational goals, community service activities, employment history and extracurricular activities. Paper applications to be mailed to: Flathead County Democratic Women     c/o Linda Harris    853 Highland Loop   Whitesh, MT 59937  (for additional information, call Linda Harris 406-261-4790)

rows.name: Whitefish Soroptimist Memorial Scholarship for Girls Graduating High School
values: Whitefish Soroptimist Memorial Scholarship for Girls Graduating High School

Eligible students: Senior girls in Flathead County Public High Schools in 2025 who are planning to attend college or university. Criteria: financial need, academic ability, and those seeking a career that aligns with the mission of Soroptimist International. Our mission statement is "A global volunteer organization that provides women and girls with access to the education and training they need to achieve economic empowerment." Priority given to girls planning to attend in-state programs (but it is NOT a requirement!).

rows.name: Whitefish Police Protective Association (2 - $1,000)
values: Recipient will be selected based upon need, academic standing and completed essay. The essay asks about the importance of law enforcement in today's society and the impact law enforcement has had in your life. The Application Committee is comprised of Whitefish Police Officers. A transcript copy and two reference letters are required. Paper applications to be dropped off in person, or mailed to: Officer Reece Stahlberg c/o Whitefish Police Department 275 Flathead Ave. Whitefish, MT 59937

rows.name: Smile Montana Scholarship ($1,000)
values: Include 1-2 page typed essay answering the following prompt: Share a personal story that will make us smile (or laugh!) Application must be submitted by April 1, 2026. Physical copies can be returned to school counselor or a digital copy can be emailed to marketing@smilemontana.com. Digital files should be a single PDF including all required documents. Please do not send word files, google doc links or multiple files.

rows.name: Montana Sheriffs & Peace Officers Association (2 - $1500)
values: MT Sheriffs & Peace Officer Association Overview

For students who are seeking a career in LOCAL law enforcement OR a current college student who is pursuing a career in LOCAL law enforcement AND whose parent is a member of MSPOA AND currently employed by a Sheriff's office in MT. Recipients will be selected on the basis of need, academic ability, and career goals. High school graduate or GED.

rows.name: P.E.O. Chapter D Scholarship (1) $1,400
values: P.E.O. is a philanthropic organization where women celebrate the advancement of women; educated women through scholarships, grants, awards, loans and motivated each other to achieve their highest aspirations. Submit applications to: P.E.O. Chapter D c/o Katherine Bachrach 816 Karrow Avenue Whitefish, MT 59937

rows.name: Montana Association of Conservation District's  2024 Natural Resources Scholarship (2 - $1,000)
values: Montana Association of Conservation District's  2024 Natural Resources Scholarship (2 - $1,000)

Must be a US citizen with Montana residency or attending an educational institution within the state of Montana; enrolled in or planning to pursue a course of study related to Montana’s natural resources. Appropriate courses of study include agriculture, agribusiness, animal science, range science, forestry, environmental science, land resource science, plant science, etc. 4 short essay questions are asked about your education, experiences, and how your course of study will allow you to have an impact on Montana’s natural resource issues in the future. Letters of recommendation, transcript, and acceptance letters (to school) are required. Contact Madi Larson at madi@macdnet.org or 406-443-5711 with questions.

rows.name: Jerry Barnes ($500)
values: Awarded to a WHS graduating senior that participated in at least one sport during senior year and attending a Montana College or Trade School. Return paper applications to Mrs. Jones by: 4/30/24.

rows.name: Student View Scholarship Program
values: Quick and easy application for a scholarship contest for high school seniors planning to attend a 2-4 year university; no application required - only completion of a survey about your local universities that takes about 15-20 minutes

rows.name: Glacier Medical Associates Scholarship Application
values: Scholarships will be awarded to graduating seniors from both WHS seeking a career in Health sciences.  Please mail your application to Glacier Medical Associates, attn. HR, 1111 Baker Avenue, Whitefish MT 59937.  Deadline April 23, 2025.

rows.name: Margaret & Jane Fellows Drama/Theatre Scholarship ($500)
values: Each year Whitefish Theatre Company presents this award to provide funds for the furthering of the recipient's education. You do NOT NEED TO MAJOR IN THEATRE TO QUALIFY; but must have past theatre-related experience. Examples might include, but are not limited to: stage crew, costume committee, pit orchestra, choreographer, improv). There are 3 essays. These can be at 250 words EACH. Return paper applications to Mrs. Jones by: 4/25/24.

rows.name: Whitefish Classified Employees Association Higher Education Scholarship
values: Whitefish Classified Employees Association Higher Education Scholarship

Your parents do NOT need to be a member of the Whitefish Classified Employees to apply; application essays are reviewed and ranked on your thoughts for your goals and plans for higher education and any special considerations as to why you should receive this scholarship. Past work history, community and school activity involvement is also considered. Application must be dropped off to front office with Eden Dias by 4/26.

rows.name: Flathead Electric Basin and MECA Scholarship (2 scholarships, 1 application!)
values: Flathead Electric Basin and MECA Scholarship (2 scholarships, 1 application!)

By completing this application, you will be considered for both scholarships. Applicant or parent/guardian must be a member of Flathead Electric Cooperative. No minimums given, but applicants will be judged on: 20% Academic Strength (as demonstrated by rigors of coursework, GPA and national testing scores), 20% Activities in School and Community, Awards & Honors, 20% Employment, Volunteerism, and Community Service and 40% Personal Statement (“Write about how your school/community/work activities will influence your goals and career choice. (600 word limit)”)

rows.name: MT Youth Serve Scholarships
values: Online Application (via Reach Higher MT portal)

Up to 90 scholarships awarded. Must have at least 100 hours of community service in the last 12 months for a $1500 scholarship. The Youth Serve Montana Scholarship was created to promote volunteerism among high school students, encourage young leaders to further their learning, and provide tuition assistance for Montana students who wish to attend college in-state.

rows.name: John & Joe Norrish Memorial Scholarship ($500-$1500)
values: Seniors graduating from accredited high schools in the Co-op’s service territory

rows.name: Reach Higher Montana Scholarship (1 application, MULTIPLE scholarships!)
values: Reach Higher Portal for Scholarships and Search Strategies
Reach Higher Montana Scholarship (1 application, MULTIPLE scholarships!)

Apply once and be considered for many Montana scholarships at the same time. Open to seniors graduating from a Montana high school who complete the FAFSA and plan to attend an accredited Montana college at least half-time. The flagship Reach Higher Montana award is $2,000 (50 given); others range about $100–$3,000. Application window: January 1 – March 1. An ideal fit for Whitefish seniors.

rows.name: Flathead Valley Community College Eagle Scholarship
values: Flathead Valley Community College Eagle Scholarship

Graduating high school senior, Completed FVCC college application. To be eligible to apply for the FVCC Eagle Scholarship, students must have applied as a new incoming, degree-seeking student for the upcoming fall semester. Running Start students can be eligible if they have earned college credits and will now be a degree-seeking student in the upcoming fall semester. Students will be awarded based on their most recent cumulative GPA (either high school or college for transfer students), HiSET or GED Scores.

rows.name: Soroptimist Certificate Scholarships
values: We are offering a new scholarship for Certificate Programs. Examples might include: local massage or cosmetology schools.  This scholarship is for women currently enrolled or considering enrolling in a program that provides a certificate instead of a degree. Applications will be reviewed monthly, and feel free to call if you have further questions.  The phone number to call is provided after you apply.

rows.name: National Farmers Union Scholarship (Minorities in Agriculture, Natural Resources and Related Sciences (MANRRS))
values: National Farmers Union Scholarship (Minorities in Agriculture, Natural Resources and Related Sciences (MANRRS))

Open to MANRRS members and their children. High school seniors, college students or nontraditional students seeking funding to attend a two or four-year accredited college or university or technical school for any area of study may apply. Recipients will be selected based on academic records, social and community activities, and a typed essay describing personal and professional goals, and involvement with MANRRS. Two $1,500 scholarships will be awarded. Application Materials Needed: 1) Completed application form. Applications may be completed electronically through Google forms or by printing out and mailing the PDF form. 2) A copy of your most recent complete academic school year’s transcript. This can be included in your application and does not need to be mailed separately by your school or university. If you are a college student, you can send an unofficial copy of your transcript that includes the current school year in addition to the previous. 3) Letters of recommendation from a MANRRS leader of your choice AND from a teacher or professor. 4) Typed essay – three pages, 12-point Times New Roman font with one-inch margins. Application Deadline: April 1, 2026. Recipients will be selected and announced by July 31, 2026.
Agriculture, Natural Resources and Related Sciences

rows.name: Adams/Marcellin International Interest Scholarship
values:
The Adams/Marcellin International Interest Scholarship, established by Greg Adams and
Colette Marcellin, is intended to help students who display an interest in global affairs, foreign
languages, or (a) culture(s) outside of their own lived experience. Paper applications to Mrs. Jones by 4/10.

rows.name: Helen Mulloy Student Scholarship ($2000)
values: 1 or more $2000 (number varies annually) scholarship(s) for seniors demonstrating financial need with a 3.5 GPA or higher attending a 4 year college or university. Full-time students maintaining a 3.5 application may renew this scholarship annually for Sophmore, Junior and Senior yr of College/University. Paper applications to Mrs. Jones by 4/3.

rows.name: Muldown Scholastic Scholarship ($1000)
values: In honor of our long-time school administrator, we award a $1000.00 scholarship to a WHS senior pursuing a career in education. The application is the SAME as the Alumni application. ONLY 1 FORM NEEDS TO BE COMPLETED, BUT WILL BE ENTERED FOR BOTH SCHOLARSHIPS. Paper application to Mrs. Jones by: 4/4.

rows.name: Whitefish High School Alumni Scholarship ($1000)
values: At the conclusion of the WHS graduating class of 1965's  50th. reunion, a fund was donated to the WEF. The Alumni Scholarship was born! It will be awarded to a WHS senior with higher education plans. The application is the SAME as the Muldown application. ONLY 1 FORM NEEDS TO BE COMPLETED, BUT WILL BE ENTERED FOR BOTH SCHOLARSHIPS. Paper application to Mrs. Jones by: 4/4.

rows.name: Whitefish Education Foundation - Community Service Scholarship  (2) $1,000
values: Whitefish Education Foundation - Community Service Scholarship  (2) $1,000

Available to Whitefish High School graduating seniors and students must have participated in some form of community service volunteerism during their high school years. This could range from volunteering at a non-profit organization to assisting an elderly neighbor. Candidates will be asked to write a brief (250 word ) essay with the prompt, “How I have impacted my community through volunteerism and what I've learned through my experience.” Return paper applications to Mrs. Jones by: 4/4/25.

rows.name: Davide Sobba Memorial Scholarship ($1,000)
values: Dr. Sobba was a dedicated orthopedic surgeon, who promoted good health and fitness. He helped found The Wave and Whitefish Ice Rink. This scholarship honors his passions despite his untimely death in 2013. Essay quality is a determining factor in selection of a winner! Return paper applications to Mrs. Jones by: 4/29/24.

rows.name: Gladys R. Spear Memorial Scholarship ($500)
values: For students with a physical or learning disability who have learned to rise above their disability. Students can be interested in pursuing life skills or post-secondary programs at vocation, trade, technical, trade school, or undergraduate education. Paper applications to Mrs. Jones by 4/4.

rows.name: Lonnie Collinsworth Scholarship
values: Generously donated by long-time Bulldog art teacher, Lonnie Collinsworth and his family, 3 short essay answers could help you win this fantastic scholarship! 1. What did you like most about your high school experience? What would you do over again? 2. Tell me a little about you and your family?   3. What are your educational plans? Typed application are due to Mrs. Jones by 4/10/25.

rows.name: Emily Leighty/DKG Lambda Scholarship ($1,000)
values: The scholarship is offered for female senior who plans to major in Education. Statement of why applicants chosen to be and Educator, resume, 2 letters of recommendation. Paper applications to Mrs. Jones by 4/3.

rows.name: Michael Kuchenbrod Scholarship
values: Personal essay approximately 500 words/one page. The essay could include some or all of the following, or could add anything the applicant feels is pertinent. Plans for further education/training Passions Community/school involvement Financial need Struggles/how you overcame Achievements (not necessarily honors) At least one letter of recommendation (no more than 2) from any adult other than a relative that knows the applicant well. Official high school transcript. Submit to Mrs. Jones by end of 5/7.

rows.name: Montana Sheriffs & Peace Officers Association (5- $1000)
values: MT Sheriffs & Peace Officer Association Overview
Child of MSPOA member scholarship application

For students whose parent is a member of MSPOA AND currently employed by a Sheriff's office in MT. Recipients will be selected on the basis of need, academic ability, and career goals. High school graduate or GED.

rows.name: Memorial Scholarship (6 awards)
values: Scholarships awarded to students based on merit, need, and extra curriculars. This award honors the WHS students who died in the 1984 bus accident.

rows.name: Sloan Sloan Memorial Scholarship for the Arts
values: Sloan Sloan Memorial Scholarship for the Arts
Sloan Sloan Memorial Scholarship for the Arts
Sloan Sloan Memorial Scholarship for the Arts

Must currently be enrolled in art or music classes; Must plan on majoring in Art or Music (2- or 4-year course); GPA not a determining factor; Have experienced or are currently experiencing hardships that have made continuing education especially challenging, including (but not limited to): Mental health struggles/PTSD; Drug or alcohol addiction; Chronic health issues; Financial problems; Unplanned pregnancy; Homelessness. Return paper applications by Friday May 1st, 2026 (handed in to Ms Ally Jones by end of day).

rows.name: P.E.O. Star Scholarship (Juniors Must Start the process this Spring for Next Year via submitting their resumes by 5/15!)
values: P.E.O. Star Scholarship (Juniors Must Start the process this Spring for Next Year via submitting their resumes by 5/15!)

Scholarship awards $2,500 to high-achieving young women who are in their final year of high school and plan to attend an accredited postsecondary educational institution in the US or Canada in the next academic year. LEADERSHIP, ACADEMICS, EXTRACURRICULAR ACTIVITIES, COMMUNITY SERVICE and potential for future success are key attributes. There are 2 Whitefish chapters and each can nominate one outstanding young woman for consideration. To apply, the process needs to start THIS YEAR via interested JUNIOR GRADE women should send an electronic copy of their resume to either Chapter BR (peomtchapterbr@gmail.com) or Chapter D (PEOchapterD.MT@gmail.com) no later than May 15. After review of resumes, each local chapter will conduct brief interviews to determine a nominee who will, in turn, complete an online application to P.E.O. International for final consideration. The online application process can start as early as August 15 but no later than October 15. Nominees are notified of the outcome in mid-April of their senior year.

rows.name: Elk's William and Sara Jenne' Scholarship Application
values: Elk's William and Sara Jenne' Scholarship Application

The recipients of these awards will be students who have completed their first year of education at a Montana University, College, Vocational Technology school or community college.  The Elks seek to encourage and assist students to complete his/her education and/or vocational training. The awards will place less emphasis on attainment of high grades than do their regular scholarship programs, and more so on the basis of need, effort, activities and community involvement.  CONDITIONS OF ELIGIBILITY: Completion of one year of study a Montana university, college, vocational technology school or community college, with at least 45 credits or 30 semester hours. Have a bonafide and verifiable need for financial assistance. Be of good morals and character. Applications should be sent to: Ryan Laqua  12906 County Road 350R  Sidney, MT 59270  Questions? Contact Ryan Laqua (406) 480-9052  rlaqua@midrivers.com

rows.name: Montana Treasure State First Generation Scholarship
values: Montana Treasure State First Generation Scholarship

This award supports first-generation Montana resident students who self-report their status on their application for admission. It is valued at $1,500 per year and is renewable for four years, and can be stacked with a Montana Premier Scholarship.

rows.name: Cat Scholarships
values: These are departmental scholarships available for qualifying students at Montana State University. Students should apply by February 1st, 2026, and explore the Cat Scholarships page for more information.

rows.name: Presidential Scholarship
values: This is Montana State University's most prestigious academic scholarship, offered by the Honors College. It cannot stack with the Premier Scholarship; if both are received, the award of higher value will be honored.

rows.name: Western Undergraduate Exchange (WUE) Tuition Discount
values: This program offers a tuition discount for students with a 3.0+ GPA who live in WUE-eligible states. Students are automatically considered if they apply by January 15, 2026, with a current high school transcript required.

rows.name: Presidential Leadership Scholarship
values: Davidson Honors College, University of Montana
This is one of the premier academic scholarships offered through the Davidson Honors College at the University of Montana.

rows.name: Provost’s Honors Scholarship
values: Davidson Honors College, University of Montana
This is one of the premier academic scholarships offered through the Davidson Honors College at the University of Montana.

rows.name: Dean’s Leadership Scholarship
values: Davidson Honors College, University of Montana
This is one of the premier academic scholarships offered through the Davidson Honors College at the University of Montana.

rows.name: Payne Family Impact Scholarship
values: This scholarship is designed for students with significant financial need who are not eligible for Federal Pell Grant. It is part of a $7.5 million scholarship fund.

rows.name: National Merit Scholarship
values: The University of Montana participates in the National Merit Scholarship Program. Awards of $2,000 a year are offered to finalists who indicate UM as their first choice, and $1,000 a year to semi-finalists who enroll.

rows.name: Grizzly Battalion Army ROTC Scholarship Program
values: Grizzly Battalion Army ROTC Scholarship Program

The University of Montana participates in the Army ROTC Scholarship program, offering two, three, and four-year scholarships. Applications are available through high school guidance offices or the UM ROTC department.

rows.name: Fly for Duke Aviation Scholarships
values: This scholarship, offered by the Duke Carrillo Foundation, provides financial assistance and mentoring to aspiring aviators aged 17 to 24. It aims to help recipients earn a private pilot's license in honor of Duke Carrillo's dream of becoming a naval aviator and professional pilot.

rows.name: NATA Richard L. Taylor Flight Training Scholarship
values: before the last Friday in March
NATA Richard L. Taylor Flight Training Scholarship

This scholarship honors Richard L. Taylor, Professor Emeritus at The Ohio State University, who significantly expanded flight education. It aims to support aviation students in furthering their careers as professional pilots.

rows.name: Strategic Partner Scholarships
values: HNTB, HDR, AECOM, Jacobs, and WSP

These scholarships are sponsored by WTS International Pinnacle and Strategic Level Corporate Partners and support the Foundation's development of students in the transportation field by encouraging bright new professionals and students to undertake careers in transportation.

rows.name: Sharon D. Banks Memorial Undergraduate Scholarship
values: Sharon D. Banks Memorial Undergraduate Scholarship

This scholarship is awarded to women pursuing undergraduate studies in transportation or a related field and honors Sharon D. Banks, general manager of Alameda-Contra Costa Transit District, who led the agency in a pioneering effort to introduce cultural and organizational changes.

rows.name: Molitoris Leadership Scholarship for Undergraduates
values: The purpose of this scholarship is to motivate and reward women who demonstrate leadership in the transportation industry, ensuring that the essential leadership skills and perspectives of women are included in planning the transportation systems of the future.

rows.name: Junior College/Trade School Scholarship
values: This scholarship fosters the development of women in the transportation field by encouraging bright new professionals to undertake careers in transportation. It is intended for students pursuing an Associate or technical degree at community and trade colleges.

rows.name: WTS Transportation YOU High School Scholarship
values: WTS Transportation YOU High School Scholarship

This scholarship is awarded to girls pursuing high school studies in science, technology, engineering, and math to foster the development of women and girls in the transportation field by encouraging bright new professionals and students to undertake careers in transportation.
Science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) related to transportation

rows.name: Kitchen Cabinet Kings 2026 Scholarship
values: The Kitchen Cabinet Kings Scholarship awards $2,500 to one U.S. college, university, or trade school student who submits the best entrepreneurship essay. Applicants must write a 500-word essay on how they would launch a small business with $10,000 and AI tools. This is a one-time award for students focused on entrepreneurship.

rows.name: Nelson Scholarship
values: Recipients of this business, interior design, and architecture scholarship will receive $1,500 to use towards expenses related to education including tuition, books, and campus housing. Students must be legal residents of the United States and be enrolled in an accredited high school, college, or university within the U.S. High school students must be entering or finishing their senior year, and college students must be enrolled for at least one full calendar year.

rows.name: Anne Ford Scholarship
values: This scholarship is granted to a graduating high school senior who will enroll in a full-time bachelor’s degree program. Applicants must have a documented learning disability (LD), and students with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) who also have a learning disability are encouraged to apply.

rows.name: Allegra Ford Thomas Scholarship
values: This scholarship is awarded to a graduating high school senior who will enroll in a two-year community college, a vocational or technical training program, or a specialized program for students with disabilities. Applicants must have a documented learning disability (LD), and students with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) and a LD are encouraged to apply.

rows.name: AOPA Foundation You Can Fly High School Flight Training Scholarship
values: The Ray Foundation – established by James C. Ray
AOPA Foundation You Can Fly High School Flight Training Scholarship

This scholarship is for high school students, aged 16-18 years old, to earn their private pilot certificate. Applicants must have a minimum GPA of 2.7 and must have passed the FAA Private Pilot written knowledge exam before application submission.

rows.name: Aircraft Lighting International Scholarship
values: This scholarship is available to a high school senior or college student. Applicants must plan to attend or be currently attending an accredited school in an avionics or aircraft maintenance program.

rows.name: James Hammond Joubert Memorial Scholarship
values: Named in memory of Jim Joubert, founder of Pacific Southwest Instruments.

Named in memory of Jim Joubert, who founded Pacific Southwest Instruments, this scholarship is available to a high school senior or college student. Applicants must plan to attend or be currently attending an accredited school in an avionics or aircraft maintenance program.

rows.name: Pat Napolitano Memorial Scholarship for Aspiring Technicians
values: In memory of Pat Napolitano, Fleet Support Representative and Staggerwing Pilot for Mid-Continent Instruments and Avionics.
Pat Napolitano Memorial Scholarship for Aspiring Technicians

This scholarship honors Pat Napolitano's legacy and passion for aircraft maintenance and flying. It is available to all graduating seniors or current college students pursuing their Aviation Technician Certification.

rows.name: David Arver Memorial Scholarship
values: Given by Dutch and Ginger Arver in memory of their son, David.

Given by Dutch and Ginger Arver in memory of their son, David, this scholarship is for a high school senior or college student. Recipients must plan to attend or be currently attending an accredited school in an avionics or aircraft maintenance program.

rows.name: Dutch and Ginger Arver Scholarship
values: This scholarship is available to a high school senior or college student who plans to attend or is attending an accredited school. The program of study must be in avionics or aircraft maintenance.

rows.name: Captain Judy Rice Pilot Scholarship
values: Epic's top pilot scholarship for U.S. high school students (juniors or seniors) who are U.S. Citizens or Permanent Residents. Applicants must be 16 years of age or older on or before December 31, 2026, and can start training within 12 months and use the scholarship within 24 months. Must have consistent, reliable transportation, parent/guardian approval if under 18, and a Third Class Medical. The student must show exemplary dedication. Can be used at any Epic campus.

rows.name: Pilot Scholarship for Flight Training
values: One of ten $5,000 scholarships for U.S. high school students (juniors or seniors) who are U.S. Citizens or Permanent Residents. Applicants must be 16 years of age or older on or before December 31, 2026, and can start training within 12 months and use the scholarship within 24 months. Must have consistent, reliable transportation, parent/guardian approval if under 18, and a Third Class Medical. To be awarded at one of Epic's flight training campuses.

rows.name: King Air Nation Pilot Scholarship for Flight Training
values: King Air Nation Pilot Scholarship for Flight Training

Scholarship for U.S. high school students (juniors or seniors) who are U.S. Citizens or Permanent Residents. Applicants must be 16 years of age or older on or before December 31, 2026, and can start training within 12 months and use the scholarship within 24 months. Must have consistent, reliable transportation, parent/guardian approval if under 18, and a Third Class Medical. Can be used at any Epic campus.

rows.name: Aircraft Mechanic Scholarship (CVG Airport)
values: One of two $20,000 scholarships for U.S. high school seniors who are U.S. Citizens or Permanent Residents. Applicants must be 18 years old by the time of completing the program, and can start training within 12 months and use the scholarship within 24 months. Must have consistent, reliable transportation and parent/guardian approval if under 18. This scholarship is awarded for training at CVG Airport.

rows.name: Aircraft Mechanic Scholarship (New Smyrna Beach)
values: One of two $20,000 scholarships for U.S. high school seniors who are U.S. Citizens or Permanent Residents. Applicants must be 18 years old by the time of completing the program, and can start training within 12 months and use the scholarship within 24 months. Must have consistent, reliable transportation and parent/guardian approval if under 18. This scholarship is awarded for training at New Smyrna Beach.

rows.name: 2024-2025 ADHD Scholarship
values: The 2024-2025 ADHD Scholarship is available for students with ADHD. Further details regarding eligibility and application requirements are accessible via the provided application link.

rows.name: HPFY Make a Difference Scholarship
values: This scholarship recognizes and rewards selfless individuals who care for those in need and give back to their communities. Applicants must be high school seniors or college students with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher and a minimum of 100 documented volunteer hours. Enrollment must be full-time in a U.S. university/college or technical college.

rows.name: Fred J. Epstein Youth Achievement Award
values: Fred J. Epstein Youth Achievement Award

This award recognizes students 19 or younger with learning disabilities and ADHD who have demonstrated initiative, talent, and determination, resulting in a notable accomplishment in any field such as art, music, science, math, athletics, or community service. It celebrates outstanding achievements and impact on schools and communities.

rows.name: Special Recognition Award
values: This special recognition award is for students 19 or younger with learning disabilities and ADHD who have demonstrated initiative, talent, and determination, resulting in a notable accomplishment in any field such as art, music, science, math, athletics, or community service. It acknowledges their outstanding achievements and impact on schools and communities.

rows.name: The Neurodiversity Scholarship
values: $1,000 or $2,500 depending on enrollment status and school type

This national scholarship supports neurodivergent students, including those with Dyslexia, ADHD, Processing Disorders, and Autism, who are between 16-26 years old and plan to enroll in an Associate, Bachelor, or Certificate program at a not-for-profit US college or university. It aims to break down financial barriers to higher education and provides access to an online community, networking, and national events.

rows.name: The Joseph James Morelli Legacy Foundation Scholarship
values: The Joseph James Morelli Legacy Foundation
The Joseph James Morelli Legacy Foundation Scholarship
This scholarship supports high school and college students with dyslexia who wish to pursue a degree in a Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics (STEM) field.

rows.name: Wells Fargo Stacey Milbern Scholarship
values: A renewable scholarship ($2,500 full-time / $1,250 half-time) for students with a disability — a long-term or recurring condition that affects a major life activity. Requires a 3.0+ GPA, U.S. citizenship or legal residency, and enrollment as a high-school senior/graduate or undergraduate at an accredited U.S. college. Only the first 700 complete applications are reviewed, so apply early.

rows.name: All-American Pest Control STEAM Trailblazer Scholarship
values: All-American Pest Control STEAM Trailblazer Scholarship

This scholarship is for female high school seniors or college/trade school students in an accredited U.S. institution. Applicants must demonstrate a strong commitment to All-American Pest Control’s core values and have a genuine passion for STEAM fields, actively pursuing or planning a career in a STEAM-related discipline. It aims to empower young women to become innovators and leaders in STEAM.
Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics (STEAM)

rows.name: Hilleman Scholars Program
values: MSU Hilleman Scholars Program, Montana State University

The Hilleman Scholars Program is for students starting at Montana State University in Fall 2026. Scholarship selection is based on a student's potential to lead and their desire to earn a college degree, as assessed by a dedicated selection committee.

rows.name: Live Your Dream Award
values: The Live Your Dream Awards offers cash awards to women who provide primary financial support for themselves and their dependents, have financial need, and are enrolled in or accepted to a vocational/skills training, high school equivalency, or an undergraduate degree program. Recipients can use the funds for tuition, books, transportation, or childcare.

rows.name: Occupational Safety and Health / Industrial Hygiene Scholarship
values: Occupational Safety and Health / Industrial Hygiene Scholarship

This scholarship is for Industrial Hygiene (IH) or Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) students who demonstrate a desire to champion safety in their chosen fields. Eligibility requires students to be enrolled full-time in good standing at an approved program.
Industrial Hygiene (IH) or Occupational Safety and Health (OSH)

rows.name: Bold $25,000 Scholarship
values: This scholarship is for undergraduate students to help cover the costs of higher education. It aims to alleviate financial burdens and support academic pursuits.

rows.name: National Technical Honor Society
values: The National Technical Honor Society annually awards five $2,000 scholarships to their members committed to pursuing careers in construction-related disciplines. Application requirements include personal information, listing of awards/honors/training participation/certifications received, a letter of recommendation, and three essay questions.

rows.name: Associated General Contractors of America’s Workforce Development Scholarship
values: Associated General Contractors of America’s Workforce Development Scholarship
This scholarship is open for students pursuing associate degrees, technical training, or certificates to enter the construction industry.

rows.name: The Kim and Harold Louie Family Foundation 2026 Scholarship
values: The Kim and Harold Louie Family Foundation
The Kim and Harold Louie Family Foundation 2026 Scholarship

The Kim and Harold Louie Family Foundation offers a scholarship for 2026. Applicants are encouraged to submit applications online, with supplemental materials like transcripts, test scores, and tax forms scanned and submitted digitally. Official copies will be requested if awarded.

rows.name: Workforce Development Scholarships
values: National Center for Construction Education and Research (NCCER) and its Build Your Future initiative, administered by AGC
Scholarships for students pursuing craft and technical programs.

rows.name: 2nd Chance Scholarships for College or Trade Schools
values: 2nd Chance Scholarships for College or Trade Schools

This scholarship is open to U.S. citizens or legal residents with a high school diploma, GED, or equivalent, who plan to attend an accredited college, university, or trade school in the U.S. in Fall 2026 or Spring 2027. There are no GPA or income requirements, and five $1,000 scholarships are awarded.

rows.name: Welder Training Scholarship
values: This scholarship is for students seeking welder training in a certificate program that is less than two years in length. It supports individuals pursuing vocational education in welding.

rows.name: Work Ethic Scholarship Program
values: The Work Ethic Scholarship Program supports U.S. citizens who are high school graduates or seniors and plan to enroll in an approved two-year or less accredited trade program. It aims to close the skills gap by assisting individuals pursuing careers in skilled trades such as welding, plumbing, electrical, and HVAC, without accumulating significant debt.

rows.name: FEC Scholarships
values: Individual scholarships range from $1,500 to $6,000. Scholarship money must be used to attend an accredited post-secondary education institution in Montana. Students eligible to apply for scholarships include: (i) Seniors graduating from accredited high schools in the Co-op’s service territory (ii) Graduating home school students (iii) Current undergraduate college students. Applicants must meet the following requirements: (i) The applicant or their parent/legal guardian must be a member of Flathead Electric Cooperative and served by the Co-op at their primary residence. (ii) Scholarship money must be used to attend an accredited post-secondary education institution in Montana (iii) To remain eligible for scholarships that renew for more than one year, students must remain enrolled consecutively each semester at an accredited post-secondary education institution in Montana.

rows.name: AFSA No Essay Scholarship Program
values: AFSA awards $1,000 scholarships to 10 students annually. Two Contests. Deadlines August & December Every Year.

rows.name: Pride Foundation Community Scholarships
values: A single application opens 60+ LGBTQ+ community scholarship funds for students who are LGBTQ+ or allies and reside in Alaska, Idaho, Montana, Oregon, or Washington. Montana residents are explicitly eligible and may study anywhere; it covers community college, 4-year, and trade/vocational study. The cycle runs roughly October to January.

rows.name: Point Foundation Flagship Scholarship
values: Point Foundation's flagship national scholarship supports LGBTQ+ students and allies and is open to applicants who are at least a high-school senior. It is a need-based award renewable for up to four years and requires a 3.3 GPA and a demonstrated connection and commitment to the LGBTQ+ community. The window runs September to late November.

rows.name: Fisher House Scholarships for Military Children
values: Fisher House Scholarships for Military Children

A $2,000 scholarship for unmarried military dependent children under age 23 with a valid military ID, whose parent is active-duty, Guard/Reserve, retired, or deceased. High-school senior applicants need a 3.0 GPA and full-time enrollment in an accredited 2- or 4-year program.

rows.name: AMVETS Children/Grandchildren Scholarship
values: For children and grandchildren of honorably discharged U.S. veterans or active military, open to 12th graders entering college the fall of their graduation year. Pays $1,000/year (up to $4,000) toward a bachelor's at an accredited 4-year school; requires demonstrated financial need (FAFSA). Window runs January through April 30.

rows.name: Montana National Guard Tuition Waiver
values: Apply via campus — by 3rd week of 1st semester
Apply through MUS campus financial aid — mus.edu/Prepare/Pay/Waivers

A last-dollar waiver covering in-state tuition for enlisted members of the Montana Army or Air National Guard in good standing who have completed Initial Entry Training. This is not a family benefit — the student themselves must be a Guard member. Apply through your MUS campus.

rows.name: War Orphans Tuition Waiver (MUS)
values: Apply via campus — by 3rd week of 1st semester
Apply through MUS campus financial aid — mus.edu/Prepare/Pay/Waivers

Waives undergraduate tuition at Montana University System campuses for Montana-resident children (age 25 or under) of service members who were Montana residents at entry to service and were killed in action or died of a service-connected cause. Cannot be combined with other waivers; does not cover fees.

rows.name: The Gates Scholarship
values: A highly selective last-dollar scholarship for Pell-eligible high-school seniors who are African American, Hispanic American, Native American/Alaska Native, or Asian & Pacific Islander American. Requires a minimum 3.3 weighted GPA and full-time enrollment in a four-year degree. (Active successor to the discontinued Gates Millennium Scholars program.)

rows.name: CSKT Higher Education Scholarship
values: Funds undergraduate and graduate study for enrolled Confederated Salish & Kootenai Tribes (CSKT) members who hold a high-school diploma or GED/HiSET and are accepted to an accredited institution. Reapply each year; applications open in January with a May 1 deadline.

rows.name: Blackfeet Nation Higher Education Program
