values: The scholarship is offered for female senior who plans to major in Education. Statement of why applicants chosen to be and Educator, resume, 2 letters of recommendation. Paper applications to Mrs. Jones by 4/3.

rows.name: Michael Kuchenbrod Scholarship
values: Personal essay approximately 500 words/one page. The essay could include some or all of the following, or could add anything the applicant feels is pertinent. Plans for further education/training Passions Community/school involvement Financial need Struggles/how you overcame Achievements (not necessarily honors) At least one letter of recommendation (no more than 2) from any adult other than a relative that knows the applicant well. Official high school transcript. Submit to Mrs. Jones by end of 5/7.

rows.name: Montana Sheriffs & Peace Officers Association (5- $1000)
values: MT Sheriffs & Peace Officer Association Overview
Child of MSPOA member scholarship application

For students whose parent is a member of MSPOA AND currently employed by a Sheriff's office in MT. Recipients will be selected on the basis of need, academic ability, and career goals. High school graduate or GED.

rows.name: Memorial Scholarship (6 awards)
values: Scholarships awarded to students based on merit, need, and extra curriculars. This award honors the WHS students who died in the 1984 bus accident.

rows.name: Sloan Sloan Memorial Scholarship for the Arts
values: Sloan Sloan Memorial Scholarship for the Arts
Sloan Sloan Memorial Scholarship for the Arts
Sloan Sloan Memorial Scholarship for the Arts

Must currently be enrolled in art or music classes; Must plan on majoring in Art or Music (2- or 4-year course); GPA not a determining factor; Have experienced or are currently experiencing hardships that have made continuing education especially challenging, including (but not limited to): Mental health struggles/PTSD; Drug or alcohol addiction; Chronic health issues; Financial problems; Unplanned pregnancy; Homelessness. Return paper applications by Friday May 1st, 2026 (handed in to Ms Ally Jones by end of day).

rows.name: P.E.O. Star Scholarship (Juniors Must Start the process this Spring for Next Year via submitting their resumes by 5/15!)
values: P.E.O. Star Scholarship (Juniors Must Start the process this Spring for Next Year via submitting their resumes by 5/15!)

Scholarship awards $2,500 to high-achieving young women who are in their final year of high school and plan to attend an accredited postsecondary educational institution in the US or Canada in the next academic year. LEADERSHIP, ACADEMICS, EXTRACURRICULAR ACTIVITIES, COMMUNITY SERVICE and potential for future success are key attributes. There are 2 Whitefish chapters and each can nominate one outstanding young woman for consideration. To apply, the process needs to start THIS YEAR via interested JUNIOR GRADE women should send an electronic copy of their resume to either Chapter BR (peomtchapterbr@gmail.com) or Chapter D (PEOchapterD.MT@gmail.com) no later than May 15. After review of resumes, each local chapter will conduct brief interviews to determine a nominee who will, in turn, complete an online application to P.E.O. International for final consideration. The online application process can start as early as August 15 but no later than October 15. Nominees are notified of the outcome in mid-April of their senior year.

rows.name: Elk's William and Sara Jenne' Scholarship Application
values: Elk's William and Sara Jenne' Scholarship Application

The recipients of these awards will be students who have completed their first year of education at a Montana University, College, Vocational Technology school or community college.  The Elks seek to encourage and assist students to complete his/her education and/or vocational training. The awards will place less emphasis on attainment of high grades than do their regular scholarship programs, and more so on the basis of need, effort, activities and community involvement.  CONDITIONS OF ELIGIBILITY: Completion of one year of study a Montana university, college, vocational technology school or community college, with at least 45 credits or 30 semester hours. Have a bonafide and verifiable need for financial assistance. Be of good morals and character. Applications should be sent to: Ryan Laqua  12906 County Road 350R  Sidney, MT 59270  Questions? Contact Ryan Laqua (406) 480-9052  rlaqua@midrivers.com

rows.name: Montana Treasure State First Generation Scholarship
values: Montana Treasure State First Generation Scholarship

This award supports first-generation Montana resident students who self-report their status on their application for admission. It is valued at $1,500 per year and is renewable for four years, and can be stacked with a Montana Premier Scholarship.

rows.name: Cat Scholarships
values: These are departmental scholarships available for qualifying students at Montana State University. Students should apply by February 1st, 2026, and explore the Cat Scholarships page for more information.

rows.name: Presidential Scholarship
values: This is Montana State University's most prestigious academic scholarship, offered by the Honors College. It cannot stack with the Premier Scholarship; if both are received, the award of higher value will be honored.

rows.name: Western Undergraduate Exchange (WUE) Tuition Discount
values: This program offers a tuition discount for students with a 3.0+ GPA who live in WUE-eligible states. Students are automatically considered if they apply by January 15, 2026, with a current high school transcript required.

rows.name: Presidential Leadership Scholarship
values: Davidson Honors College, University of Montana
This is one of the premier academic scholarships offered through the Davidson Honors College at the University of Montana.

rows.name: Provost’s Honors Scholarship
values: Davidson Honors College, University of Montana
This is one of the premier academic scholarships offered through the Davidson Honors College at the University of Montana.

rows.name: Dean’s Leadership Scholarship
values: Davidson Honors College, University of Montana
This is one of the premier academic scholarships offered through the Davidson Honors College at the University of Montana.

rows.name: Payne Family Impact Scholarship
values: This scholarship is designed for students with significant financial need who are not eligible for Federal Pell Grant. It is part of a $7.5 million scholarship fund.

rows.name: National Merit Scholarship
values: The University of Montana participates in the National Merit Scholarship Program. Awards of $2,000 a year are offered to finalists who indicate UM as their first choice, and $1,000 a year to semi-finalists who enroll.

rows.name: Grizzly Battalion Army ROTC Scholarship Program
values: Grizzly Battalion Army ROTC Scholarship Program

The University of Montana participates in the Army ROTC Scholarship program, offering two, three, and four-year scholarships. Applications are available through high school guidance offices or the UM ROTC department.

rows.name: Fly for Duke Aviation Scholarships
values: This scholarship, offered by the Duke Carrillo Foundation, provides financial assistance and mentoring to aspiring aviators aged 17 to 24. It aims to help recipients earn a private pilot's license in honor of Duke Carrillo's dream of becoming a naval aviator and professional pilot.

rows.name: NATA Richard L. Taylor Flight Training Scholarship
values: before the last Friday in March
NATA Richard L. Taylor Flight Training Scholarship

This scholarship honors Richard L. Taylor, Professor Emeritus at The Ohio State University, who significantly expanded flight education. It aims to support aviation students in furthering their careers as professional pilots.

rows.name: Strategic Partner Scholarships
values: HNTB, HDR, AECOM, Jacobs, and WSP

These scholarships are sponsored by WTS International Pinnacle and Strategic Level Corporate Partners and support the Foundation's development of students in the transportation field by encouraging bright new professionals and students to undertake careers in transportation.

rows.name: Sharon D. Banks Memorial Undergraduate Scholarship
values: Sharon D. Banks Memorial Undergraduate Scholarship

This scholarship is awarded to women pursuing undergraduate studies in transportation or a related field and honors Sharon D. Banks, general manager of Alameda-Contra Costa Transit District, who led the agency in a pioneering effort to introduce cultural and organizational changes.

rows.name: Molitoris Leadership Scholarship for Undergraduates
values: The purpose of this scholarship is to motivate and reward women who demonstrate leadership in the transportation industry, ensuring that the essential leadership skills and perspectives of women are included in planning the transportation systems of the future.

rows.name: Junior College/Trade School Scholarship
values: This scholarship fosters the development of women in the transportation field by encouraging bright new professionals to undertake careers in transportation. It is intended for students pursuing an Associate or technical degree at community and trade colleges.

rows.name: WTS Transportation YOU High School Scholarship
values: WTS Transportation YOU High School Scholarship

This scholarship is awarded to girls pursuing high school studies in science, technology, engineering, and math to foster the development of women and girls in the transportation field by encouraging bright new professionals and students to undertake careers in transportation.
Science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) related to transportation

rows.name: Kitchen Cabinet Kings 2026 Scholarship
values: The Kitchen Cabinet Kings Scholarship awards $2,500 to one U.S. college, university, or trade school student who submits the best entrepreneurship essay. Applicants must write a 500-word essay on how they would launch a small business with $10,000 and AI tools. This is a one-time award for students focused on entrepreneurship.

rows.name: Nelson Scholarship
values: Recipients of this business, interior design, and architecture scholarship will receive $1,500 to use towards expenses related to education including tuition, books, and campus housing. Students must be legal residents of the United States and be enrolled in an accredited high school, college, or university within the U.S. High school students must be entering or finishing their senior year, and college students must be enrolled for at least one full calendar year.

rows.name: Anne Ford Scholarship
values: This scholarship is granted to a graduating high school senior who will enroll in a full-time bachelor’s degree program. Applicants must have a documented learning disability (LD), and students with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) who also have a learning disability are encouraged to apply.

rows.name: Allegra Ford Thomas Scholarship
values: This scholarship is awarded to a graduating high school senior who will enroll in a two-year community college, a vocational or technical training program, or a specialized program for students with disabilities. Applicants must have a documented learning disability (LD), and students with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) and a LD are encouraged to apply.

rows.name: AOPA Foundation You Can Fly High School Flight Training Scholarship
values: The Ray Foundation – established by James C. Ray
AOPA Foundation You Can Fly High School Flight Training Scholarship

This scholarship is for high school students, aged 16-18 years old, to earn their private pilot certificate. Applicants must have a minimum GPA of 2.7 and must have passed the FAA Private Pilot written knowledge exam before application submission.

rows.name: Aircraft Lighting International Scholarship
values: This scholarship is available to a high school senior or college student. Applicants must plan to attend or be currently attending an accredited school in an avionics or aircraft maintenance program.

rows.name: James Hammond Joubert Memorial Scholarship
values: Named in memory of Jim Joubert, founder of Pacific Southwest Instruments.

Named in memory of Jim Joubert, who founded Pacific Southwest Instruments, this scholarship is available to a high school senior or college student. Applicants must plan to attend or be currently attending an accredited school in an avionics or aircraft maintenance program.

rows.name: Pat Napolitano Memorial Scholarship for Aspiring Technicians
values: In memory of Pat Napolitano, Fleet Support Representative and Staggerwing Pilot for Mid-Continent Instruments and Avionics.
Pat Napolitano Memorial Scholarship for Aspiring Technicians

This scholarship honors Pat Napolitano's legacy and passion for aircraft maintenance and flying. It is available to all graduating seniors or current college students pursuing their Aviation Technician Certification.

rows.name: David Arver Memorial Scholarship
values: Given by Dutch and Ginger Arver in memory of their son, David.

Given by Dutch and Ginger Arver in memory of their son, David, this scholarship is for a high school senior or college student. Recipients must plan to attend or be currently attending an accredited school in an avionics or aircraft maintenance program.

rows.name: Dutch and Ginger Arver Scholarship
values: This scholarship is available to a high school senior or college student who plans to attend or is attending an accredited school. The program of study must be in avionics or aircraft maintenance.

rows.name: Captain Judy Rice Pilot Scholarship
values: Epic's top pilot scholarship for U.S. high school students (juniors or seniors) who are U.S. Citizens or Permanent Residents. Applicants must be 16 years of age or older on or before December 31, 2026, and can start training within 12 months and use the scholarship within 24 months. Must have consistent, reliable transportation, parent/guardian approval if under 18, and a Third Class Medical. The student must show exemplary dedication. Can be used at any Epic campus.

rows.name: Pilot Scholarship for Flight Training
values: One of ten $5,000 scholarships for U.S. high school students (juniors or seniors) who are U.S. Citizens or Permanent Residents. Applicants must be 16 years of age or older on or before December 31, 2026, and can start training within 12 months and use the scholarship within 24 months. Must have consistent, reliable transportation, parent/guardian approval if under 18, and a Third Class Medical. To be awarded at one of Epic's flight training campuses.

rows.name: King Air Nation Pilot Scholarship for Flight Training
values: King Air Nation Pilot Scholarship for Flight Training

Scholarship for U.S. high school students (juniors or seniors) who are U.S. Citizens or Permanent Residents. Applicants must be 16 years of age or older on or before December 31, 2026, and can start training within 12 months and use the scholarship within 24 months. Must have consistent, reliable transportation, parent/guardian approval if under 18, and a Third Class Medical. Can be used at any Epic campus.

rows.name: Aircraft Mechanic Scholarship (CVG Airport)
values: One of two $20,000 scholarships for U.S. high school seniors who are U.S. Citizens or Permanent Residents. Applicants must be 18 years old by the time of completing the program, and can start training within 12 months and use the scholarship within 24 months. Must have consistent, reliable transportation and parent/guardian approval if under 18. This scholarship is awarded for training at CVG Airport.

rows.name: Aircraft Mechanic Scholarship (New Smyrna Beach)
values: One of two $20,000 scholarships for U.S. high school seniors who are U.S. Citizens or Permanent Residents. Applicants must be 18 years old by the time of completing the program, and can start training within 12 months and use the scholarship within 24 months. Must have consistent, reliable transportation and parent/guardian approval if under 18. This scholarship is awarded for training at New Smyrna Beach.

rows.name: 2024-2025 ADHD Scholarship
values: The 2024-2025 ADHD Scholarship is available for students with ADHD. Further details regarding eligibility and application requirements are accessible via the provided application link.

rows.name: HPFY Make a Difference Scholarship
values: This scholarship recognizes and rewards selfless individuals who care for those in need and give back to their communities. Applicants must be high school seniors or college students with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher and a minimum of 100 documented volunteer hours. Enrollment must be full-time in a U.S. university/college or technical college.

rows.name: Fred J. Epstein Youth Achievement Award
values: Fred J. Epstein Youth Achievement Award

This award recognizes students 19 or younger with learning disabilities and ADHD who have demonstrated initiative, talent, and determination, resulting in a notable accomplishment in any field such as art, music, science, math, athletics, or community service. It celebrates outstanding achievements and impact on schools and communities.

rows.name: Special Recognition Award
values: This special recognition award is for students 19 or younger with learning disabilities and ADHD who have demonstrated initiative, talent, and determination, resulting in a notable accomplishment in any field such as art, music, science, math, athletics, or community service. It acknowledges their outstanding achievements and impact on schools and communities.

rows.name: The Neurodiversity Scholarship
values: $1,000 or $2,500 depending on enrollment status and school type

This national scholarship supports neurodivergent students, including those with Dyslexia, ADHD, Processing Disorders, and Autism, who are between 16-26 years old and plan to enroll in an Associate, Bachelor, or Certificate program at a not-for-profit US college or university. It aims to break down financial barriers to higher education and provides access to an online community, networking, and national events.

rows.name: The Joseph James Morelli Legacy Foundation Scholarship
values: The Joseph James Morelli Legacy Foundation
The Joseph James Morelli Legacy Foundation Scholarship
This scholarship supports high school and college students with dyslexia who wish to pursue a degree in a Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics (STEM) field.

rows.name: Wells Fargo Stacey Milbern Scholarship
values: A renewable scholarship ($2,500 full-time / $1,250 half-time) for students with a disability — a long-term or recurring condition that affects a major life activity. Requires a 3.0+ GPA, U.S. citizenship or legal residency, and enrollment as a high-school senior/graduate or undergraduate at an accredited U.S. college. Only the first 700 complete applications are reviewed, so apply early.

rows.name: All-American Pest Control STEAM Trailblazer Scholarship
values: All-American Pest Control STEAM Trailblazer Scholarship

This scholarship is for female high school seniors or college/trade school students in an accredited U.S. institution. Applicants must demonstrate a strong commitment to All-American Pest Control’s core values and have a genuine passion for STEAM fields, actively pursuing or planning a career in a STEAM-related discipline. It aims to empower young women to become innovators and leaders in STEAM.
Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics (STEAM)

rows.name: Hilleman Scholars Program
values: MSU Hilleman Scholars Program, Montana State University

The Hilleman Scholars Program is for students starting at Montana State University in Fall 2026. Scholarship selection is based on a student's potential to lead and their desire to earn a college degree, as assessed by a dedicated selection committee.

rows.name: Live Your Dream Award
values: The Live Your Dream Awards offers cash awards to women who provide primary financial support for themselves and their dependents, have financial need, and are enrolled in or accepted to a vocational/skills training, high school equivalency, or an undergraduate degree program. Recipients can use the funds for tuition, books, transportation, or childcare.

rows.name: Occupational Safety and Health / Industrial Hygiene Scholarship
values: Occupational Safety and Health / Industrial Hygiene Scholarship

This scholarship is for Industrial Hygiene (IH) or Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) students who demonstrate a desire to champion safety in their chosen fields. Eligibility requires students to be enrolled full-time in good standing at an approved program.
Industrial Hygiene (IH) or Occupational Safety and Health (OSH)

rows.name: Bold $25,000 Scholarship
values: This scholarship is for undergraduate students to help cover the costs of higher education. It aims to alleviate financial burdens and support academic pursuits.

rows.name: National Technical Honor Society
values: The National Technical Honor Society annually awards five $2,000 scholarships to their members committed to pursuing careers in construction-related disciplines. Application requirements include personal information, listing of awards/honors/training participation/certifications received, a letter of recommendation, and three essay questions.

rows.name: Associated General Contractors of America’s Workforce Development Scholarship
values: Associated General Contractors of America’s Workforce Development Scholarship
This scholarship is open for students pursuing associate degrees, technical training, or certificates to enter the construction industry.

rows.name: The Kim and Harold Louie Family Foundation 2026 Scholarship
values: The Kim and Harold Louie Family Foundation
The Kim and Harold Louie Family Foundation 2026 Scholarship

The Kim and Harold Louie Family Foundation offers a scholarship for 2026. Applicants are encouraged to submit applications online, with supplemental materials like transcripts, test scores, and tax forms scanned and submitted digitally. Official copies will be requested if awarded.

rows.name: Workforce Development Scholarships
values: National Center for Construction Education and Research (NCCER) and its Build Your Future initiative, administered by AGC
Scholarships for students pursuing craft and technical programs.

rows.name: 2nd Chance Scholarships for College or Trade Schools
values: 2nd Chance Scholarships for College or Trade Schools

This scholarship is open to U.S. citizens or legal residents with a high school diploma, GED, or equivalent, who plan to attend an accredited college, university, or trade school in the U.S. in Fall 2026 or Spring 2027. There are no GPA or income requirements, and five $1,000 scholarships are awarded.

rows.name: Welder Training Scholarship
values: This scholarship is for students seeking welder training in a certificate program that is less than two years in length. It supports individuals pursuing vocational education in welding.

rows.name: Work Ethic Scholarship Program
values: The Work Ethic Scholarship Program supports U.S. citizens who are high school graduates or seniors and plan to enroll in an approved two-year or less accredited trade program. It aims to close the skills gap by assisting individuals pursuing careers in skilled trades such as welding, plumbing, electrical, and HVAC, without accumulating significant debt.

rows.name: FEC Scholarships
values: Individual scholarships range from $1,500 to $6,000. Scholarship money must be used to attend an accredited post-secondary education institution in Montana. Students eligible to apply for scholarships include: (i) Seniors graduating from accredited high schools in the Co-op’s service territory (ii) Graduating home school students (iii) Current undergraduate college students. Applicants must meet the following requirements: (i) The applicant or their parent/legal guardian must be a member of Flathead Electric Cooperative and served by the Co-op at their primary residence. (ii) Scholarship money must be used to attend an accredited post-secondary education institution in Montana (iii) To remain eligible for scholarships that renew for more than one year, students must remain enrolled consecutively each semester at an accredited post-secondary education institution in Montana.

rows.name: AFSA No Essay Scholarship Program
values: AFSA awards $1,000 scholarships to 10 students annually. Two Contests. Deadlines August & December Every Year.

rows.name: Pride Foundation Community Scholarships
values: A single application opens 60+ LGBTQ+ community scholarship funds for students who are LGBTQ+ or allies and reside in Alaska, Idaho, Montana, Oregon, or Washington. Montana residents are explicitly eligible and may study anywhere; it covers community college, 4-year, and trade/vocational study. The cycle runs roughly October to January.

rows.name: Point Foundation Flagship Scholarship
values: Point Foundation's flagship national scholarship supports LGBTQ+ students and allies and is open to applicants who are at least a high-school senior. It is a need-based award renewable for up to four years and requires a 3.3 GPA and a demonstrated connection and commitment to the LGBTQ+ community. The window runs September to late November.

rows.name: Fisher House Scholarships for Military Children
values: Fisher House Scholarships for Military Children

A $2,000 scholarship for unmarried military dependent children under age 23 with a valid military ID, whose parent is active-duty, Guard/Reserve, retired, or deceased. High-school senior applicants need a 3.0 GPA and full-time enrollment in an accredited 2- or 4-year program.

rows.name: AMVETS Children/Grandchildren Scholarship
values: For children and grandchildren of honorably discharged U.S. veterans or active military, open to 12th graders entering college the fall of their graduation year. Pays $1,000/year (up to $4,000) toward a bachelor's at an accredited 4-year school; requires demonstrated financial need (FAFSA). Window runs January through April 30.

rows.name: Montana National Guard Tuition Waiver
values: Apply via campus — by 3rd week of 1st semester
Apply through MUS campus financial aid — mus.edu/Prepare/Pay/Waivers

A last-dollar waiver covering in-state tuition for enlisted members of the Montana Army or Air National Guard in good standing who have completed Initial Entry Training. This is not a family benefit — the student themselves must be a Guard member. Apply through your MUS campus.

rows.name: War Orphans Tuition Waiver (MUS)
values: Apply via campus — by 3rd week of 1st semester
Apply through MUS campus financial aid — mus.edu/Prepare/Pay/Waivers

Waives undergraduate tuition at Montana University System campuses for Montana-resident children (age 25 or under) of service members who were Montana residents at entry to service and were killed in action or died of a service-connected cause. Cannot be combined with other waivers; does not cover fees.

rows.name: The Gates Scholarship
values: A highly selective last-dollar scholarship for Pell-eligible high-school seniors who are African American, Hispanic American, Native American/Alaska Native, or Asian & Pacific Islander American. Requires a minimum 3.3 weighted GPA and full-time enrollment in a four-year degree. (Active successor to the discontinued Gates Millennium Scholars program.)

rows.name: CSKT Higher Education Scholarship
values: Funds undergraduate and graduate study for enrolled Confederated Salish & Kootenai Tribes (CSKT) members who hold a high-school diploma or GED/HiSET and are accepted to an accredited institution. Reapply each year; applications open in January with a May 1 deadline.

rows.name: Blackfeet Nation Higher Education Program
values: A higher-education grant for enrolled members of the Blackfeet Tribe pursuing an undergraduate degree or certificate at an accredited institution; requires certification of Blackfeet blood. Awards are roughly $2,800–$3,000 with a March 1 deadline. (Confirm amount with the Blackfeet Education Department.)

rows.name: Louise A. Dean All Montana Tribal Nations Scholarship
values: Louise A. Dean All Montana Tribal Nations Scholarship

A need-based scholarship for members of any Montana tribal nation (Assiniboine, Blackfeet, Gros Ventre, Chippewa Cree, Crow, Kootenai, Little Shell, Northern Cheyenne, Pend d'Oreille, Salish, or Sioux) pursuing a certificate, associate, or bachelor's degree. Open to graduating high-school seniors; requires a 2.25 GPA and proof of financial need. Window Jan 1 to Mar 31.

rows.name: Montana American Indian Tuition Waiver
values: Covers undergraduate tuition at Montana University System campuses for enrolled members or tribally certified descendants of a federally recognized tribe located in Montana. Requires demonstrated financial need (at least $1 of remaining need) and about 12 months of Montana residency; covers tuition only, not fees. Renewable annually.

rows.name: NFPA (National Foster Parent Association) Scholarship
values: A $500 award for graduating high-school seniors (or GED completers), ages 17 to 21, in foster care, kinship care, adoptive, or resource families. Note the gate: the applicant's parent or another supportive adult must be a current NFPA member.

rows.name: Adoption STAR Academic Scholarship
values: Three annual awards ($1,000 / $750 / $500) for college-bound students who were adopted or spent time in foster care and plan to attend a 4-year college. Selection weighs character, overcoming adversity, and academic progress. Due May 31.

rows.name: Montana Foster Youth Higher Education Assistance Program
values: Montana Foster Youth Higher Education Assistance Program
Apply through your MUS campus financial aid office (foster youth / federal Chafee program)

Last-dollar assistance for Montana foster youth eligible for the federal John H. Chafee program. Must enroll full-time in a degree, vocational, or entry-level professional credential program, have 12 months Montana residency, and have graduated high school or earned an equivalency. Apply through your MUS campus financial aid office.

rows.name: Coca-Cola Scholars Program
values: An achievement- and leadership-based $20,000 award; 150 high-school seniors are selected each year. Open to all graduating seniors (not restricted by background) with a minimum 3.0 GPA. The application window runs August to September 30.

rows.name: Dell Scholars Program
values: A $20,000 scholarship (plus laptop, textbook credits, and emergency aid) for Pell-eligible high-school seniors who participated in an approved college-readiness program in grades 11-12 and plan to enroll full-time at a four-year college. Rewards persistence over grades — minimum GPA is 2.4. Due February 15. Note the gate: you must have been in an approved college-readiness / college-access program.

rows.name: Heroes' Legacy Scholarship (Fisher House)
values: For children of service members who died or became seriously injured in the line of duty since 9/11. Administered by Fisher House Foundation through the military scholarship portal (militaryscholar.org); a military-dependent / veteran-family award for graduating seniors entering an accredited college.

rows.name: Montana STEM/Healthcare Scholarship Program
values: Annual — closes Mar 15 (apply after fall acceptance)

For Montana high school seniors from Board of Public Education accredited schools pursuing a qualifying STEM or Healthcare major, enrolling full-time at an eligible Montana campus the fall after graduation. Requires 3.25 cumulative GPA plus 4 years college-prep math and 3 years college-prep science. STEM-focused, renewable annually if requirements are met.

rows.name: Montana FFA Foundation Leave a Legacy Scholarship
values: Montana FFA Foundation Leave a Legacy Scholarship

Open to any Montana FFA member pursuing post-secondary education or trade/technical school. FFA membership is the gating criterion; a single unified application through the Reach Higher Montana portal qualifies applicants for all Montana FFA Foundation scholarships. Graduating high school FFA seniors are eligible.

rows.name: Rhino Roofing 2026 Scholarship
values: Annual — closes noon (12 PM) Mon Apr 6, 2026

Seven $1,000 scholarships for 2026 graduating high school seniors from Flathead, Lake, Missoula, or Ravalli Counties in Montana with a minimum 3.0 GPA, usable toward tuition, books, or expenses at any accredited college or trade school. Local/trades sponsor; apply by emailing the application plus a 500-word essay to Sherry@RhinoRoofingMt.com.

rows.name: Bernard Greufe Memorial Honor Scholarship
values: A $1,500 award administered by the Montana Farm Bureau Foundation to assist Montana Farm Bureau members and children of members pursuing higher education. Farm Bureau membership/family affiliation is the gating criterion; agriculture-oriented. Graduating high school seniors who are members or children of members are eligible.

rows.name: Montana Farm Bureau Women's Leadership Committee Scholarships
values: Montana Farm Bureau Federation — Women's Leadership Committee
Montana Farm Bureau Women's Leadership Committee Scholarships

Two $1,500 scholarships from the MFB Women's Leadership Committee, available to both boys and girls graduating high school, who must be a current paid Montana Farm Bureau member or an immediate member of a current paid Montana Farm Bureau family. Agriculture/Farm Bureau affiliation is the gating criterion.

rows.name: MABA-MGEA Scholarship
values: Montana FFA Foundation (endowed by Montana Agri-Business Assn. & Montana Grain Elevator Assn.)

A $500 scholarship for Montana FFA members planning to study agriculture or the agricultural products industry (ag-business, grain industry, agri-business fields). Requires FFA membership and at least 2 years of agricultural education classes. Graduating high school FFA seniors in Montana are eligible; apply via the unified Reach Higher Montana / Montana FFA application.

rows.name: National FFA Scholarship Program
values: One online application on the Kaleidoscope portal considers current FFA members for 120+ National FFA scholarships. Graduating high school seniors who are current FFA members qualify (under 23, planning to attend a US college, university, or trade school). Awards run up to $10,000 each.

rows.name: EAA Ray Aviation Scholarship
values: Varies by local EAA chapter (chapters selected annually; no single national deadline)
National; administered through local EAA chapters (student must connect with a participating chapter)

This aviation scholarship funds up to $12,000 toward a private/sport pilot certificate for youth ages 16-19 (15 for glider). Candidates are selected by a participating local EAA chapter, then screened by EAA — so a Whitefish senior must engage a chapter, complete a Young Eagles flight, and hold a student pilot certificate. High-school seniors in the age range qualify.

rows.name: American Welding Society (AWS) Idaho/Montana Section Scholarships
values: Annual — opens Dec 1, closes Mar 1 (for the following fall term)
Regional — students in Idaho or Montana; AWS Idaho/Montana Section
American Welding Society (AWS) Idaho/Montana Section Scholarships

The AWS Idaho/Montana Section funds welding/trades students in ID or MT pursuing a welding degree or certificate at a 2-year or 4-year school. A graduating Whitefish senior qualifies as an incoming welding student (AWS requires HS graduate/GED status by the fall term). One AWS Foundation online application at scholarship.aws.org covers National, District, and Section awards.

rows.name: Lineman Country Scholarship (Southeast Lineman Training Center)
values: National; Southeast Lineman Training Center (SLTC), Trenton, GA
Lineman Country Scholarship (Southeast Lineman Training Center)

This trades/lineman scholarship from Southeast Lineman Training Center awards $5,000 (five awards in 2026) to individuals starting a career in the electrical utility/communications lineworker industry. A graduating high school senior or GED holder planning a lineman career qualifies; applicants submit letters of recommendation from three references and an essay to the Scholarship Committee.

rows.name: International Lineman's Rodeo Association (ILRA) Scholarship
values: Varies (set yearly by the ILRA Board; covers tuition, textbooks, fees)

This lineman/trades scholarship is for a son or daughter of a Journeyman Lineman OR someone recommended by one, entering accredited lineman training. Applicants need a high school diploma or GED, so a graduating Whitefish senior qualifies via the family/sponsor connection. Two recommendation letters (one from a HS/GED advisor) and a personal financial-need statement are required.

rows.name: NESA Scholarships (National Eagle Scout Association)
values: Annual — opens Dec 1, closes Jan 31 (11:59pm CST)
National; open to Eagle Scouts nationwide

NESA scholarships are for Eagle Scouts and require NESA membership. They explicitly open to graduating high school seniors: Eagle Scouts may apply beginning in their senior year of high school. Awards range from a $5,000 Tappan Scholarship up to a $50,000 four-year Cooke Scholarship ($12,500/yr), with a hard filter on Eagle Scout / Scouting status.

rows.name: Donald Runnicles Musical Arts Scholarship Competition (Grand Teton Music Festival)
values: Annual — spring (2026 deadline extended to Mon May 18)
Regional — Wyoming, Idaho, and Montana residents; competition held in Jackson, WY
Donald Runnicles Musical Arts Scholarship Competition (Grand Teton Music Festival)

The Donald Runnicles Musical Arts Scholarship Competition is a regional music award open to graduating high school seniors from Wyoming, Idaho or Montana who are pursuing a music degree in college. Montana is explicitly included, so a Whitefish HS senior planning a music degree fits. Selection is by video pre-screen then live semi-final/final rounds, with prizes of $10,000–$25,000.

rows.name: ESA Foundation Computer & Video Game Arts Scholarship
values: Annual — opens Apr 1, closes Apr 30 (11:59 PT)
National (US citizens); administered via Kaleidoscope online portal
ESA Foundation Computer & Video Game Arts Scholarship

For students pursuing video-game, interactive-entertainment and STEAM careers, this esports/gaming award supports future game creators. Applicants may be graduating HS seniors entering a four-year undergraduate program in fall 2026. Priority to women, nonbinary/gender-nonconforming, or economically disadvantaged applicants.
Video game arts / STEAM / interactive entertainment

rows.name: ESA Foundation Esports Scholarship
values: Annual — opens Apr 1, closes Apr 30 (11:59 PT)
National (US citizens); administered via Kaleidoscope online portal

This esports award supports students competing on or managing a college esports team/club, or those confirmed to compete at the collegiate level in fall 2026. A graduating HS senior can qualify if they are confirmed to compete on a college esports team in fall 2026 (a self-selected filter, not an ineligibility bar). Full-time four-year undergraduate enrollment, min 2.5 GPA, US citizenship, and financial need apply.

rows.name: Vegetarian Resource Group (VRG) Scholarship
values: National (US high school seniors); mail/email application to VRG, Baltimore, MD

The Vegetarian Resource Group awards students graduating from US high schools who have promoted vegetarianism/veganism in their schools and communities. This vegetarian/vegan-focused award grants one $10,000 and five $5,000 scholarships. Requires transcripts, three-plus recommendation letters, and an essay on advocacy and goals.

rows.name: Duck Brand "Stuck at Prom" Scholarship Contest
values: Annual — submit by early June (2026: Jun 3, 12 PM ET)
National (US, DC, PR, territories; excludes MD, CO, NE, ND — Montana eligible)
Duck Brand "Stuck at Prom" Scholarship Contest

This creative/contest scholarship is a photo CONTEST, not a traditional essay scholarship: entrants make and wear original promwear from Duck Tape and submit a photo, judged on creativity and execution. Open to students 14+ enrolled at the high-school level during the 2025-2026 school year. Grand prizes are $10,000 per category with $1,000 runner-up and special-category awards.

rows.name: 2026 Montana 4-H Scholarship
values: Annual — closes Feb 14 (not shown on live portal page)

A single Kaleidoscope portal application covering all Montana 4-H Foundation scholarships for Montana students with 4-H involvement (typically 3+ years in 4-H). 4-H membership is the gating criterion. Applicants complete one application and are matched to the scholarships they qualify for; graduating high school seniors are eligible.

rows.name: FIRST Scholarship Portal (Pearson Futures)
values: Varies (most due senior year of HS, Dec–Apr)
National; online portal (futures.pearson.com/scholarships) aggregating FIRST partner scholarships

The FIRST Scholarship program is a robotics/FIRST portal (hosted on Pearson Futures) linking graduating high school seniors who did FRC/FTC/FLL to 150+ partner scholarships from colleges, businesses, and associations. It is a dynamic portal, not a single award: each scholarship has its own amount, eligibility, process, and deadline. HS seniors are explicitly the target audience.

rows.name: GBCI Leadership Scholarship
values: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26GBBS) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/gbci-leadership-scholarship

For children, step-children, and employees of Glacier Bancorp (GBCI, headquartered in Kalispell, MT); full- or part-time students eligible. Corporate-sponsor employee/dependent scholarship. Typical award $2,000 per year.

rows.name: Dearborn Ranch Montana Game Wardens Scholarship
values: Dearborn Ranch Montana Game Wardens Scholarship
Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26DRSFGW) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/dearborn-ranch-montana-game-wardens-scholarship
For biological or adopted children of active uniformed Montana Fish, Wildlife & Parks Game Wardens (a law-enforcement / first responder family scholarship). Typical award $10,000 per year.

rows.name: Dearborn Ranch Montana Highway Patrol Scholarship
values: Dearborn Ranch Montana Highway Patrol Scholarship
Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26DRSFHP) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/dearborn-ranch-montana-highway-patrol-scholarship
For biological or adopted children of active uniformed Montana Highway Patrol officers (a first responder / law-enforcement family scholarship). Minimum cumulative GPA 2.75. Award $10,000 per year.

rows.name: Kay McMillan Nursing Scholarship
values: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26KMSE) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/kay-mcmillan-nursing-scholarship

For graduating seniors enrolling in the pre-nursing program at Montana Tech (or current Montana Tech pre-nursing / nursing students) who show a commitment to community health. Minimum high-school GPA 2.0. Typical award $500–$1,500 per year. Nursing / healthcare focus.

rows.name: Alan & Janette Blackburn Scholarship
values: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26BLAK) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/alan-and-janette-blackburn-scholarship

Open to any student who graduated or will graduate from a Montana high school, awarded through the Montana Community Foundation. Typical award $500–$1,000 per year. Applies to Whitefish, MT graduating seniors statewide.

rows.name: Nep & Mary Ellen Lynch Trade School Scholarship
values: Nep & Mary Ellen Lynch Trade School Scholarship
Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26NMES) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/nep-mary-ellen-lynch-trade-school-scholarship

For current graduating seniors and past graduates of Montana high schools enrolling full- or part-time at an accredited Montana trade school (cosmetology and massage schools are ineligible). Trade / vocational focus. Typical award $5,000 per year.

rows.name: T. Eugene Young Montana's Promise Scholarship
values: T. Eugene Young Montana's Promise Scholarship
Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26TEYS) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/t-eugene-young-montanas-promise-scholarship
For graduating Montana high school seniors pursuing STEM (science, technology, engineering, mathematics) or healthcare degrees to strengthen Montana's workforce. Typical award $1,000–$1,500 per year.

rows.name: Reach for the Future Scholarship for Vocational Degree Programs
values: Reach for the Future Scholarship for Vocational Degree Programs
Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26VMSE2YR) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/reach-for-the-future-scholarship-for-vocational-degree-programs

For Montana residents (or those with strong Montana ties) enrolled — or seeking enrollment — full-time at a public, private, or tribal college in Montana, studying a vocational or trade program such as aviation technology, carpentry, welding, automobile mechanics, or plumbing. Financial need required. Two-year renewable award, $2,500 per year (must maintain a 2.5 GPA to renew).
Vocational, Trades (welding, aviation technology, carpentry, plumbing)

rows.name: Gary Olszewski Memorial Scholarship
values: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26GOMS) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/gary-olszewski-memorial-scholarship

For students enrolling in a two-year technical / trade program at an accredited school; honors a Montana dryland farmer-tradesman to encourage careers in the trades (carpentry, plumbing, electrical, mechanics). Typical award $8,000 per year for two years. Open statewide, with a preference for Blaine/Hill/Phillips County students.

rows.name: Equitable Excellence Scholarship
values: $5,000/year, renewable up to 4 years ($20,000 total); up to 100 awards

National merit scholarship from Equitable (administered by Scholarship America) for U.S. high school seniors with a 2.5+ GPA planning full-time enrollment in a two- or four-year college. $5,000 per year, renewable up to four years ($20,000 total); up to 100 awards. Annual cycle typically opens September and closes December.

rows.name: NAEHCY Scholarship
values: Minimum five awards of $1,000 each (per student)

National NAEHCY Scholar Fund award for students who are or have been homeless and are McKinney-Vento eligible. Open to college-bound graduating seniors and postsecondary students under 23; a minimum of five $1,000 awards, usable at any accredited U.S. college. 2026 deadline July 31 (recurs annually).

rows.name: Name of Scholarship
values: Accepts Gap Year Applications Upon Return
rows.rationale: Workbook header/context preserved as reference, not an award or action authority.

rows.name: STATE UNIVERSITY SCHOLARSHIPS
values: This entry refers to a collection of scholarships offered by a State University, previously identified and applied to by WHS students. It serves as a historical reference, and applicants must verify current details through provided links.

rows.name: Montana’s STEM/Healthcare Scholarship Program
values: This scholarship provides an incentive for Montana high school students to pursue degrees in STEM and Healthcare fields. Applicants must be Montana residents, have a 3.25 GPA, complete specific high school courses, and enroll full-time in a qualifying major at an eligible MUS campus immediately after high school graduation.

rows.name: Montana State University (MSU) Scholarship Homepage
values: This is the official scholarship homepage for Montana State University (MSU). It provides a central resource for students to explore and apply for various scholarships offered by the university.

rows.name: Montana Resident Freshman Scholarships
values: This scholarship is specifically for Montana residents who are incoming freshman students. It is part of a reference guide compiled from past scholarship searches by mentors and WHS students.

rows.name: CAT Scholarships (Departmental +more)
values: This entry refers to various departmental scholarships available through the Montana AcademicWorks portal. Students are encouraged to explore the portal for specific scholarship opportunities.

rows.name: UM Academic Achievement Scholarship
values: This scholarship is automatically considered for new students pursuing their first bachelor's degree when they apply for admission to the University of Montana. It is awarded based on academic achievement.

rows.name: Western Undergraduate Exchange
values: The Western Undergraduate Exchange (WUE) program offers a tuition discount to students with a 3.0+ GPA who live in WUE-eligible states. Students are automatically considered if they apply for admission by January 15, 2026.

rows.name: Davidson Honors College Scholarships (Presidential Leadership Scholarship, Provost’s Honors Scholarship, Dean’s Leadership Scholarship)
values: Davidson Honors College, University of Montana
Davidson Honors College Scholarships (Presidential Leadership Scholarship, Provost’s Honors Scholarship, Dean’s Leadership Scholarship)

These are premier academic scholarships offered through the Davidson Honors College at the University of Montana. They include the Presidential Leadership Scholarship, Provost’s Honors Scholarship, and the Dean’s Leadership Scholarship, designed for high-achieving students.

rows.name: Grizzly Promise
values: The Grizzly Promise ensures that tuition is covered for in-state residents from families with an income of $50,000 or less. This program is dedicated to making college affordable for eligible Montana students.

rows.name: Scholarship Universe
values: Scholarship Universe is an online portal used by the University of Montana to help students find, apply for, and accept scholarship opportunities across campus. Students can complete matching questions to find scholarships they qualify for and manage their applications.

rows.name: Payne Family Impact Scholarship
values: This scholarship is funded by a $7.5 million fund and is designed for students with significant financial need. It targets those who are not eligible for Federal Pell Grants, aiming to provide support where other federal aid may not reach.

rows.name: Athletic Scholarships
values: The University of Montana offers athletic scholarships and degree-completion scholarships for student-athletes. These scholarships total over $4.2 million and support more than 300 student-athletes across various intercollegiate sports.

rows.name: National Merit Scholarship
values: University of Montana (participates in National Merit Scholarship Program)

The University of Montana participates in the National Merit Scholarship Program, offering awards to finalists and semi-finalists. Finalists who designate UM as their first choice receive $2,000 annually, while semi-finalists enrolling at UM receive $1,000 annually.

rows.name: Grizzly Battalion ROTC (Army ROTC Scholarship program)
values: University of Montana Army ROTC department
Grizzly Battalion ROTC (Army ROTC Scholarship program)

The University of Montana participates in the Army ROTC Scholarship program through its Grizzly Battalion. Four-year scholarship applications are available via high school guidance offices, while two and three-year scholarships can be obtained directly from the UM ROTC department.

rows.name: Horatio Alger Montana Scholarship Program
values: Dennis and Phyllis Washington Foundation (Sponsor), University of Montana (for students aspiring to attend)

The Horatio Alger Montana Scholarship Program offers financial assistance to eligible high school seniors in Montana. This scholarship supports students who aspire to pursue higher education at the University of Montana, provided through the Dennis and Phyllis Washington Foundation.

rows.name: Montana Community Foundation Portal
values: The Montana Community Foundation (MCF) offers over 50 scholarship opportunities through an online Scholarship Portal. Applicants must create an account and can take an Eligibility Quiz to match with suitable scholarships. Applications are accepted electronically only.

rows.name: Pell Promise for Montana Students
values: This financial aid initiative enhances accessibility and affordability for Montana residents. It provides significant financial assistance to Federal Pell Grant recipients from Montana who maintain a GPA of 3.0 or higher, reside on-campus, and accept a federal Stafford loan. The scholarship covers tuition only.

rows.name: Gianforte Trade and Technology Scholarships
values: $1,500 for full-time or $750 for part-time enrollment

This scholarship provides $1,500 for full-time or $750 for part-time enrollment for students in technical and trade-focused programs. Applicants must be Montana residents, file a FAFSA, have unmet financial need, maintain satisfactory academic progress, and be enrolled in at least 6 credits in a qualifying program at an eligible campus.

rows.name: FVCC Donor-Funded Scholarships
values: Apply for over 850 institutional scholarships offered by FVCC. These scholarships range from $250 to $10,000 and can be based on merit, financial need, or other criteria.

rows.name: FVCC Academic Scholarship
values: This scholarship waives in-district tuition for two semesters. It is awarded to high-achieving FVCC students.

rows.name: FVCC Eagle Scholarship
values: This scholarship provides $500-$1,000 for new incoming, degree-seeking students. It is awarded based on academic merit.

rows.name: STEM Experience and National Science Foundation Scholarship
values: STEM Experience and National Science Foundation Scholarship
This scholarship offers up to $10,000 per year for students exploring STEM career paths. It is a need-based scholarship.

rows.name: High School Honors Tuition Waiver
values: This waiver is for high school seniors who graduate from certain high schools in the top 10 percent of their class. It provides an in-district tuition waiver for two semesters.

rows.name: Northwest Montana Attendance Area Waiver
values: This waiver is for the top high school graduate from certain high schools in the Northwest Montana attendance area. It provides an in-district tuition waiver for two semesters.

rows.name: Sons of Norway Transfer Scholarship
values: This scholarship provides up to $2,500 for FVCC graduates transferring to Montana State University or University of Montana. Preference is given to candidates who have demonstrated community service.

rows.name: C.K. Logue Transfer Scholarship
values: This scholarship offers $1,000-$2,000 for FVCC graduates transferring to a four-year institution. Applicants must demonstrate financial need.

rows.name: Jarecki Foundation Loan Repayment
values: This program provides up to $5,000 in post-graduation loan repayment assistance. It is available for FVCC AAS, CAS, and CTS graduates or completers.

rows.name: 2+2 Honor Scholarship
values: This scholarship provides a two-year tuition waiver to any four-year Montana University System campus. It is transferable between campuses.

rows.name: Gianforte Trade and Technology Scholarships
values: This scholarship provides $750-$1,500 for Montana residents. It supports students pursuing trade or technology programs.

rows.name: Montana National Guard Tuition Waiver
values: This program offers tuition assistance for eligible Montana National Guard members. It provides a tuition waiver.

rows.name: American Indian Waiver
values: This program provides tuition assistance for persons of at least one-quarter (1/4) Indian blood or enrolled members of recognized Indian tribes. Applicants must demonstrate financial need.

rows.name: Montana University System Honor Scholarship
values: This is a four-year renewable scholarship that waives the recipient’s tuition. It can be used at an eligible campus within the Montana University System.

rows.name: Outside Scholarships
values: Many scholarships are offered by various community groups to support students who wish to attend college. The amounts and criteria for these scholarships vary.

rows.name: MUS Honor Scholarship
values: Montana University System, Office of the Commissioner of Higher Education

The MUS Honor Scholarship is a 4-year renewable tuition waiver for high-achieving Montana high school graduates. Applicants must have a minimum 3.4 GPA, meet rigorous core requirements, and be accepted by an eligible Montana University System campus. It aims to support students pursuing higher education within Montana.

rows.name: WUE Schools
values: WICHE (Western Interstate Commission for Higher Education)

The Western Undergraduate Exchange (WUE) program allows students from WICHE member states to enroll in participating two-year and four-year public college programs outside of their home state at a reduced tuition rate, typically 150% of the in-state tuition.

rows.name: Military Scholarship
values: This scholarship is intended for students pursuing military-related studies or service.

rows.name: Fastweb's $2,026 Scholarship Success Sweepstakes!
values: This is a sweepstakes offered by Fastweb, a free scholarship search platform. Students can enter to win a $2,026 scholarship. Fastweb connects students to college and trade school scholarships and financial aid resources.

rows.name: Blue Collar Brain Scholarship Program
values: This scholarship is for students pursuing education in a skilled trade. Applicants must be US citizens or have a student visa, be a high school graduate or GED recipient, and plan to enroll full-time in a vocational/technical school or 2-year college for the fall 2025 semester, maintaining a GPA of 3.0 or higher.
Skilled Trade (e.g., automotive, aviation, carpentry, construction, electrical, HVAC, plumbing, welding)

rows.name: 2025 AMVETS & WD40 Company Veteran Scholarship Program
values: 2025 AMVETS & WD40 Company Veteran Scholarship Program

Scholarships for veterans, spouses of veterans, active-duty service members, and spouses of active-duty service members to pursue training and certification in construction trades. Applicants must have a high school diploma or GED and be enrolled in an eligible construction trades program.

rows.name: The Brendan Looney Foundation Camp Scholarships
values: one month prior to the start date
The Brendan Looney Foundation Camp Scholarships

Provides financial support for children aged 17 and under of Active-Duty, Wounded Warriors, and Gold Star Children/Siblings to attend academic, athletic, art, music, or leadership camps. Scholarships are paid directly to the camp.
Academic, Athletic, Art, Music, Leadership/Exploration Camps

rows.name: The Brendan Looney Foundation High School Senior Scholarships
values: The Brendan Looney Foundation High School Senior Scholarships

A one-time scholarship for High School Seniors attending a 4-year college in Fall. Eligibility includes Gold Star Children & Siblings, and children of wounded warriors or active-duty members of the armed forces.

rows.name: The Brendan Looney Foundation College Scholarships
values: The Brendan Looney Foundation College Scholarships

A one-time scholarship offered anytime during a student's 4 years of college. Eligibility includes Gold Star Children & Siblings, and children of wounded warriors or active-duty members of the armed forces.

rows.name: Bunker Labs Veterans in Residence Program
values: Bunker Labs via D’Aniello Institute for Veterans & Military Families, Syracuse University
Bunker Labs Veterans in Residence Program

A 10-week virtual program for veterans, military spouses, and life partners (Post 9/11 service, honorable discharge) focusing on entrepreneurship. The program is offered at no cost to participants and requires 5-8 hours per week commitment.

rows.name: All Other
values: Mentors through past searches with other WHS students

This scholarship entry represents a collection of past scholarships identified by Mentors and WHS students. It serves as a reference guide for previous research efforts. Applicants must validate current status and details through provided links.

rows.name: The Kim and Harold Louie Family Foundation Scholarship Program
values: The Kim and Harold Louie Family Foundation
The Kim and Harold Louie Family Foundation Scholarship Program

This scholarship is for high school seniors and incoming freshmen attending a college or university in the United States. Applicants should demonstrate outstanding personal achievements, academic merit, leadership, and/or community service. Special consideration is given to those with U.S. veteran parents, demonstrated financial need, or first-generation college parents.

rows.name: Colorado State University First Generation Award
values: Colorado State University First Generation Award

The Colorado State University First Generation Award is for students who demonstrate financial need, are admitted to CSU by March 1, and whose parents did not receive bachelor's degrees. Applicants must be newly admitted to a degree program at CSU-Fort Collins, be a Colorado resident or in-state resident, a US citizen or eligible noncitizen, and enrolled full-time.

rows.name: Editor World First-Generation Student Scholarship
values: The Editor World First-Generation Student Scholarship offers $500 to first-generation graduate students enrolled in a master's or doctoral program in the U.S. Applicants must submit a 900-word essay detailing academic success and the relationship between resources and education. Funds can be used for educational expenses like books and supplies.

rows.name: Ryan McAuliffe Memorial Award
values: This scholarship aims to support young Hispanic female high school students in Illinois as they prepare for college. Applicants with financial need and community service experience who will be first-generation college students are preferred. The scholarship helps them achieve their professional goals.
Hispanic, Female-identifying, Community Service, First-generation college student (preferred)

rows.name: Skylar's Hope Scholarship
values: This scholarship honors the memory of Skylar Holly by supporting students passionate about helping others and making the world safer. It is for high school seniors, undergraduate, or trade school students pursuing a career as a first responder (firefighter, police, EMT, etc.).

rows.name: Virginia Douglas Memorial Scholarship for Change
values: Rape Incest Survivor Empowerment United Project
Virginia Douglas Memorial Scholarship for Change

This scholarship supports students pursuing careers in social work or related fields, striving to make a difference in preventing and addressing sexual violence. It is open to high school, undergraduate, or graduate students who are Missouri residents. First-generation students, underrepresented minorities, and single parents are strongly encouraged to apply.
Social work or a related field, First-generation students, underrepresented minorities, single parents (encouraged)

rows.name: Fuiava Engineering Scholarship
values: This scholarship supports Samoan students pursuing higher education in engineering. It is open to high school or undergraduate students ready to take on the challenge of engineering.

rows.name: Andrew Lopez Anesthesia Scholarship
values: This scholarship aims to honor the life of Andrew Lopez by supporting doctoral students who embody his perseverance and determination. It is specifically for those pursuing nurse anesthesia.

rows.name: Adam Montes Pride Scholarship
values: This scholarship aims to honor the life of Adam Montes by supporting underrepresented students on the road to higher education. It is for LGBTQ+ and underrepresented minority first-generation college students (high school senior, undergraduate, or graduate).
LGBTQ+, underrepresented minority, first-generation college student

rows.name: Sharen and Mila Kohute Scholarship
values: Ohio, Pennsylvania, West Virginia, or Virginia

This scholarship seeks to honor Sharen and Mila Kohute by supporting first-generation female students who are committed to pursuing higher education. Applicants must be high school seniors or undergraduates from Ohio, Pennsylvania, West Virginia, or Virginia.

rows.name: Maurice Geyen Business Scholarship
values: This scholarship aims to honor the life of Maurice Geyen by supporting African American male students who have experienced the foster care system. It is open to high school or undergraduate students pursuing a business field of study.
Business, African American, Male-identifying, foster care system experience

rows.name: James Lynn Baker II #BeACoffeeBean Scholarship
values: The Good Samaritan at the Baker Estate

This scholarship seeks to honor the life and legacy of Mr. Baker by supporting African American students in Texas who are pursuing higher education. A volunteering background is preferred for applicants who are high school seniors or undergraduates.

rows.name: A Heroes Family Scholarship
values: This scholarship provides financial support for a student who has lost a parent/guardian or spouse to an on-duty tragedy of a first responder (law-enforcement, fire, or military). It is open to high school seniors or above.
Lost a parent/guardian or spouse in the line of duty including those in law-enforcement, fire, or military

rows.name: DC's Opportunity Grant
values: Greater Los Angeles Region in California

This scholarship aims to empower low-income, first-generation students in the Greater Los Angeles Region in California to pursue high-demand trade careers. It is for high school seniors or graduates planning to attend trade school (HVAC, plumbing, electric, automotive repair, etc.).
First-generation college student, low-income, trade school (HVAC, plumbing, electric, automotive repair, etc.)

rows.name: Lori Nethaway Memorial Scholarship
values: This scholarship will support a female high school senior in California who is a first-generation college student. It aims to help them pursue higher education.

rows.name: Spaghetti and Butter Scholarship
values: This scholarship aims to support first-generation high school seniors in North Carolina so they can overcome the hurdles they face and achieve their goals in higher education. Applicants must have a 3.0 GPA or higher.

rows.name: Se Vale Soñar Scholarship
values: This scholarship aims to provide financial support to Hispanic/Latinx first-generation college students in Arizona so that they can thrive. It is open to high school seniors or undergraduate students.

rows.name: Gomez Family Legacy Scholarship
values: This scholarship seeks to support underserved Hispanic students in Texas so they can have the resources they need to pursue higher education. It is for high school juniors or seniors who are first-generation and/or low-income.

rows.name: Saswati Gupta Cancer Research Scholarship
values: This scholarship aims to support female students interested in medicine or biology so they can go on to advance cancer research and prevention. It is open to undergraduate juniors or seniors, or graduate students.
Medicine or Biology, Female, Cancer Research

rows.name: Rio Rico High School First-Generation Student Scholarship
values: Rio Rico High School First-Generation Student Scholarship
This scholarship aims to help first-generation high school seniors from Rio Rico High School in Arizona make the leap from high school to college so they can succeed in all of their endeavors.
First-generation college student, Rio Rico High School

rows.name: Be Great NC Scholarship
values: This scholarship aims to support first-generation college students who are underrepresented minorities in North Carolina. It assists them in earning their degrees so they can pay it forward to future generations of their families.

rows.name: Mark D. Schwarck Memorial Scholarship
values: This scholarship aims to honor the memory of Mark D. Schwarck by supporting high school seniors in Iowa who have encountered barriers in their pursuit of higher education. It helps students who have overcome adversity.

rows.name: New Jersey New York First Generation Scholarship
values: New Jersey New York First Generation Scholarship

This scholarship seeks to help two first-generation college students, from New Jersey or New York, pay for college. Applicants must be high school seniors or undergraduate students with a minimum 3.5 GPA and low-income background.

rows.name: Aserina Hill Memorial Scholarship
values: This scholarship aims to preserve Aserina Hill’s legacy of giving by providing financial aid to high school seniors with non-profit or community service experience. It gives students the opportunity to attend college.

rows.name: DeJean Legacy Scholarship For Haitian American Students
values: DeJean Legacy Scholarship For Haitian American Students
This scholarship aims to support Haitian American high school seniors who aspire to pursue a college degree so they can achieve all of their goals. Applicants must have a 3.2 GPA or higher.

rows.name: Losinger Nursing Scholarship
values: This scholarship aims to honor the lifetime of dedication of Mary Lou Losinger by supporting students who share her passion for nursing. It is open to high school seniors or current undergraduates.

rows.name: Sunshine Legall Scholarship
values: This scholarship seeks to give underrepresented BIPOC high school seniors the resources they need to pursue higher education and all of the opportunities that come with it. Applicants must have a 2.0 GPA or higher.

rows.name: Minority/BIPOC Students in STEM Scholarship
values: This scholarship seeks to support underrepresented BIPOC high school or undergraduate students in Oregon, Idaho, or Washington as they prepare to pursue their college education. It is for those studying environmental or civil engineering, geology, or environmental science.
Environmental or civil engineering, geology, or environmental science, BIPOC

rows.name: Hospitality Futures Scholarship
values: This scholarship aims to address the underrepresentation of Black students in hospitality programs by providing financial assistance and fostering a more inclusive industry. It is for high school seniors or undergraduate students in Tennessee with financial need.
Hospitality and tourism management, African American

rows.name: Maynard and Adonna Moreland Scholarship
values: Friends of the Moreland and Rawson families

This scholarship seeks to honor the lives of Maynard and Adonna Moreland by supporting first-generation high school seniors from East Career Technical Academy in Nevada. It assists students who need help pursuing higher education.
First-generation student, East Career Technical Academy

rows.name: Jimmy Cardenas Community Leader Scholarship
values: This scholarship aims to help undergraduate students in Texas who are interested in pursuing a career that serves their community. It is open to undergraduate students or those in trade school.
Career of Interest: Must be interested in serving your community via your career

rows.name: Dream BIG, Rise HIGHER Scholarship
values: This scholarship seeks to support high school seniors or undergraduate students pursuing higher education in order to make a difference and build a better tomorrow. Applicants must have a 2.5 GPA or higher.

rows.name: Aaron Libson Champion of Human Rights Scholarship
values: Aaron Libson Champion of Human Rights Scholarship

This scholarship aims to honor the incredible legacy of Aaron Libson by supporting first-generation college students in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, who share his commitment to fighting for their beliefs. It is for high school seniors or graduates starting college Fall of 2026, pursuing social work, education, healthcare, public service, environmental studies, or law.
First-generation college student, social work, education, healthcare, public service, environmental studies, or law

rows.name: Dr. Christine Lawther First in the Family Scholarship
values: Bold.org (in honor of Dr. Christine Lawther)
Dr. Christine Lawther First in the Family Scholarship
This scholarship is for students who are the first in their family to attend college. It aims to support first-generation students in pursuing higher education.

rows.name: STEAM Generator Scholarship
values: This scholarship aims to make college more accessible to students with no family background in higher education. It supports first or second-generation immigrants or other underrepresented minorities pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in a STEAM field. Applicants should share their hopes and fears about pursuing college and how their background has affected their education and goals.

rows.name: Dr. Michael Paglia Scholarship
values: Dr. Michael Paglia and Dr. Albina Claps-Paglia

This scholarship honors the lives of Dr. Michael Paglia and Dr. Albina Claps-Paglia by helping first-generation undergraduate or graduate students from lower socioeconomic status overcome financial barriers. Applicants must be pursuing a degree in the field of healthcare and demonstrate ambition, drive, and financial need.

rows.name: Li Family Scholarship
values: This scholarship supports Asian American high school seniors who are first-generation college students. It aims to make higher education more accessible by providing financial assistance. Applicants need to write an essay about their Asian American background and their motivation for pursuing higher education.

rows.name: Soroptimist's Live Your Dream Award
values: The Soroptimist's Live Your Dream Awards program provides education awards for women who are the primary financial support for their families. It offers resources to improve their education, skills, and employment prospects, supporting enrollment in vocational training or undergraduate degree programs.

rows.name: Dell Scholars Program
values: The Dell Scholars program provides financial assistance, academic advising, and career coaching to 500 students nationwide each year. It aims to help students earn their bachelor's degree by offering a flexible scholarship for tuition, housing, books, and living expenses. Eligibility requires being a high school senior in an approved college readiness program, planning to enroll full-time in a four-year college, being Pell Grant eligible, and having a minimum 2.4 GPA.

rows.name: George M. Pullman Educational Foundation Scholarship
values: George M. Pullman Educational Foundation Scholarship

This scholarship supports high school seniors from Cook County, Illinois, who demonstrate strong financial need and academic achievement. It provides up to $10,000 per year for four years to students enrolling full-time in a bachelor's degree program. Scholars are expected to succeed academically and professionally, be active in their communities, and overcome challenges.

rows.name: KPMG Future Leaders Program
values: The KPMG Future Leaders Program is a charitable initiative designed to increase the diversity pipeline of women in business and STEM fields. It awards female high school seniors annual scholarships, ongoing development, mentorship, and an introduction to golf. Eligibility requires demonstrated financial need, U.S. citizenship, and academic excellence.

rows.name: All-Around Person
values: This scholarship is for students who demonstrate well-rounded qualities and achievements. It aims to recognize individuals who excel in various aspects of their academic and extracurricular lives.

rows.name: Ralph Halverson Scholarships
values: Two $1,600 scholarships are available for Montana graduating senior athletes. This fund honors Ralph Halverson, former Executive Director of the Montana Coaches Association, and was initially funded by Mark Reed, a former GFHS track & field athlete mentored by Ralph.

rows.name: Frontier Conference Scholarships
values: Two $1,500 scholarships are provided by the Frontier Conference for athletes selected by MCA Scholarship criteria. Recipients must be Montana graduating senior athletes who will attend one of the Frontier Conference Schools, including Carroll College, College of Idaho, Eastern Oregon University, Montana State University-Northern, Montana Tech, Rocky Mountain College, Southern Oregon University, University of Providence, and Montana Western.

rows.name: Montana Coaches Association Scholarships
values: Four $1,000 scholarships are awarded by the Montana Coaches Association to assist Montana graduating senior athletes. These scholarships are for athletes selected by MCA Scholarship criteria.

rows.name: Athletics
values: This entry refers to past athletic scholarships identified by mentors for WHS students. It serves as a reference guide for previous research efforts, with current status needing validation.

rows.name: 2025 AOPA FOUNDATION AVIATION/ FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAM
values: 2025 AOPA FOUNDATION AVIATION/ FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAM

This scholarship program supports high school students and teachers pursuing aviation and flight training. Applicants must be current AOPA members, complete an online application, and submit transcripts with an unweighted GPA. Teachers must be full-time employees utilizing the AOPA Foundation High School Aviation STEM Curriculum.

rows.name: AOPA Flight Training Scholarships
values: The AOPA Foundation offers scholarships to AOPA members to help them pursue primary flight training, advanced ratings, certificates, or aviation careers. Awards range from $250 to $14,000 and are open to US, DC, Canada, Guam, Puerto Rico, and US Virgin Islands residents. Applicants submit one general application to be matched with eligible scholarships.

rows.name: THE ALLYN J. CARUSO AVIATION SCHOLARSHIP
values: The friends and family of Allyn J. Caruso
THE ALLYN J. CARUSO AVIATION SCHOLARSHIP

This scholarship, established by the friends and family of Allyn J. Caruso, awards approximately $5,000 for primary aviation certification. Preference is given to active students from Maine, aged 16-26, pursuing aviation careers such as pilot, A&P mechanic, flight dispatcher, airport manager, or aircraft engineer.
Aviation, Pilot, A&P mechanic, flight dispatcher, airport manager, aircraft engineer

rows.name: AOPA FOUNDATION SCHOLARSHIP
values: Funded by generous donations, this AOPA Foundation scholarship offers $2,500 and up for primary pilot certification (Sport, Recreational or Private Pilot certificate). Applicants must be at least 16 years old at the time of application and hold a student pilot certificate.
Primary Pilot Certification (Sport, Recreational or Private Pilot certificate)

rows.name: AOPA FOUNDATION YOU CAN FLY HIGH SCHOOL FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP
values: AOPA FOUNDATION YOU CAN FLY HIGH SCHOOL FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP

The Ray Foundation offers at least 90 scholarships of $12,000 each for high school students aged 16-18 to earn their Private Pilot Certificate. Applicants must have a minimum GPA of 2.7 and must have passed the FAA Private Pilot written knowledge exam before application submission.

rows.name: AOPA FOUNDATION YOU CAN FLY TEACHER FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP
values: AOPA FOUNDATION YOU CAN FLY TEACHER FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP

The Ray Foundation offers up to 10 scholarships of $12,000 each for current, full-time teachers utilizing the AOPA Foundation High School Aviation STEM Curriculum to earn their Private Pilot Certificate. Applicants must have passed the FAA Private Pilot written knowledge exam before application submission.
Private Pilot Certificate, Aviation STEM Curriculum

rows.name: THE ALLIANCE TEXAS AOPA AVIATION SCHOLARSHIPS
values: H. Ross Perot Jr. via the AllianceTexas Foundation
THE ALLIANCE TEXAS AOPA AVIATION SCHOLARSHIPS

The AllianceTexas Foundation offers two flight training scholarships ($14,000 each) and two aviation maintenance scholarships ($2,700 each) for high school students in Northwest ISD or Eagle Mountain Saginaw ISD in Fort Worth, TX.
