Flight training is for 11th graders (16+ years old), and maintenance is for 10th or 11th graders.

rows.name: ASHTABULA COUNTY AVIATION EDUCATION INITIATIVE SCHOLARSHIPS
values: ASHTABULA COUNTY AVIATION EDUCATION INITIATIVE SCHOLARSHIPS

Dwight and Susan Bowden offer multiple $5,000 scholarships for Private Pilot Certificates. Recipients must be residents of Ashtabula County, OH, and high school students between the ages of 16 and 18 at the time of the award.

rows.name: THE BRIAN COUPE MEMORIAL FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP
values: The friends and family of Brian Coupe
THE BRIAN COUPE MEMORIAL FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP

Established by the friends and family of Brian Coupe, this scholarship offers at least $5,000 for primary flight certification. It is available for females aged 18-24 residing in Maryland, Virginia, or the District of Columbia.

rows.name: THE BRUCE W. ALATARY MEMORIAL FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP
values: The Alatary family in memory of Bruce Alatary
THE BRUCE W. ALATARY MEMORIAL FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP

The Alatary family offers this scholarship in memory of Bruce Alatary for primary pilot certification (Sport, Recreational, or Private Pilot certificate). Preference is given to female applicants training in the Morris County, New Jersey area.
Primary Certification (Sport, Recreational, or Private Pilot certificate)

rows.name: THE CARLSBAD JET CENTER AND SONOMA JET CENTER GENERAL AVIATION PROFESSIONAL SCHOLARSHIPS
values: Sonoma Aviation (Sonoma Jet Center and Carlsbad Jet Center)
THE CARLSBAD JET CENTER AND SONOMA JET CENTER GENERAL AVIATION PROFESSIONAL SCHOLARSHIPS

Sonoma Aviation offers two $6,000 awards for individuals pursuing careers in general aviation, such as Flight Dispatcher, FBO Manager, Airport Manager, Aircraft Engineer, A&P mechanic, or aircraft pilot. Applicants must be currently employed full or part-time by an aviation Fixed Base Operator (FBO) in the United States.
Flight Dispatcher, FBO Manager, Airport Manager, Aircraft Engineer, A&P mechanic, aircraft pilot, general aviation

rows.name: THE CECI STRATFORD FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP
values: Ceci Stratford of Simi Valley, California
THE CECI STRATFORD FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP

Ceci Stratford offers two $5,000+ scholarships: one for primary pilot certification (Sport, Recreational, or Private Pilot certificate) and one for an advanced rating. Applicants must be female and at least 16 years old at the time of application submission.
Primary Pilot Certification (Sport, Recreational or Private Pilot certificate), Advanced Rating

rows.name: THE CORPORATE AIRCRAFT ASSOCIATION PREFERRED FBO EMPLOYEE SCHOLARSHIP
values: THE CORPORATE AIRCRAFT ASSOCIATION PREFERRED FBO EMPLOYEE SCHOLARSHIP

The Corporate Aircraft Association offers 200 awards of $2,000 each for any aviation education purpose. Recipients must be an employee of a CAA-preferred FBO at the time of the award, and one required recommendation must come from the general manager of the CAA-preferred FBO.

rows.name: THE DANIEL T. TAUSSIG MEMORIAL FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP
values: Brenton Taussig in memory of Daniel T. Taussig
THE DANIEL T. TAUSSIG MEMORIAL FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP

Brenton Taussig offers this scholarship in memory of Daniel T. Taussig for primary pilot certification (Sport, Recreational, or Private Pilot certificate). Applicants must be at least 16 years old at the time of application submission.
Primary certification (Sport, Recreational or Private Pilot certificate)

rows.name: THE DAVID & FLORENCE KLEINE FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP
values: David Kleine, in memory of his beloved wife, Florence
THE DAVID & FLORENCE KLEINE FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP

David Kleine offers a $5,000 scholarship in memory of Florence Kleine for primary pilot certification (Sport, Recreational, or Private Pilot certificate). Applicants must be at least 16 years old, with preference given to those training in Illinois or Minnesota.
Primary certification (Sport, Recreational or Private Pilot certificate)

rows.name: THE DUDLEY D. AND DELORES R. MALONE MEMORIAL FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP
values: The Dudley D. and Delores R. Malone Family Foundation
THE DUDLEY D. AND DELORES R. MALONE MEMORIAL FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP

The Dudley D. and Delores R. Malone Family Foundation offers four $5,000 scholarships for primary pilot certification (Sport, Recreational, or Private Pilot certificate). Applicants must be at least 16 years old, with two scholarships awarded to females and two to males.
Primary certification (Sport, Recreational or Private Pilot certificate)

rows.name: THE EDWARD B. SHAFER FUTURE OF FLIGHT SCHOLARSHIP
values: Paul Guse in memory of Edward B. Shafer
THE EDWARD B. SHAFER FUTURE OF FLIGHT SCHOLARSHIP

Paul Guse offers a $5,000 scholarship in memory of Edward B. Shafer for students pursuing an aviation career, including aerospace engineering, professional pilot, flight instruction, aircraft maintenance, and airport management. Applicants must be currently enrolled at an accredited university or college, with preference given to those in the mid-west United States, females, and minorities.
Aviation, Aerospace Engineering, Professional Pilot, Flight Instruction, Aircraft Maintenance, Airport Management

rows.name: ERRAL LEA AND GLENN PLYMATE MEMORIAL FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP
values: Glenn Plymate and his family in memory of Erral Lea Plymate, and later Glenn Plymate
ERRAL LEA AND GLENN PLYMATE MEMORIAL FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP

This memorial scholarship, established by Glenn Plymate and his family, offers multiple awards of $2,500 and up for primary pilot certification (Sport, Recreational, or Private Pilot certificate). It honors Erral Lea and Glenn Plymate's legacy and passion for aviation.
Primary certification (Sport, Recreational or Private Pilot certificate)

rows.name: THE FRED AND DIANE FITTS MEMORIAL FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP BY CAA
values: Corporate Aircraft Association (CAA) in memory of Fred and Diane Fitts
THE FRED AND DIANE FITTS MEMORIAL FLIGHT TRAINING SCHOLARSHIP BY CAA

The Corporate Aircraft Association offers $7,500 scholarships in memory of Fred and Diane Fitts for private pilot certification or instrument rating. Applicants must be aged 17-35, with preference given to those interested in becoming corporate pilots, CAA members/relatives, and employees/relatives of CAA-preferred FBOs.
Private pilot certification or instrument rating, Corporate Pilot

rows.name: THE JULIE WALKER IBRAHIM "WINGS OF OPPORTUNITY" SCHOLARSHIP FOR WOMEN IN AVIATION
values: THE JULIE WALKER IBRAHIM "WINGS OF OPPORTUNITY" SCHOLARSHIP FOR WOMEN IN AVIATION

Julie Walker Ibrahim offers a $5,000 scholarship to support young women pursuing flight training toward a Private Pilot Certificate or Instrument Rating. Eligible applicants are high school or college female students with a GPA of 2.8 or greater.
Private Pilot Certificate or Instrument Rating

rows.name: THE RICHARD MCSPADDEN SCHOLARSHIP FOR ADVANCED PILOT TRAINING
values: Multiple donors in memory of AOPA Air Safety Institute Senior Vice President Richard McSpadden
THE RICHARD MCSPADDEN SCHOLARSHIP FOR ADVANCED PILOT TRAINING

Funded by multiple donors in memory of Richard McSpadden, this scholarship supports advanced pilot training such as tailwheel, upset recovery, or other advanced ratings. The quantity and amount of awards will vary, aiming to create better, safer pilots.
Advanced Pilot Training (tailwheel, upset recovery, other advanced ratings)

rows.name: THE RICHARD SANTORI MEMORIAL SCHOLARSHIP
values: Dr. Gina Santori, in memory of her husband Richard Santori

Dr. Gina Santori offers a $6,000 scholarship in memory of her husband Richard Santori for primary pilot certification (Sport, Recreational, or Private Pilot certificate). The scholarship aims to encourage and support young people in pursuing recreational aviation and aviation careers.
Primary certification (Sport, Recreational or Private Pilot certificate), Recreational Aviation, Aviation Careers

rows.name: SENATOR JAMES M. INHOFE FAA KNOWLEDGE TEST SCHOLARSHIP
values: The State Chamber of Oklahoma in honor of Senator Inhofe
SENATOR JAMES M. INHOFE FAA KNOWLEDGE TEST SCHOLARSHIP

The State Chamber of Oklahoma offers multiple $250 awards in honor of Senator Inhofe to cover the testing fee for the FAA Private Pilot Knowledge Exam or FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Knowledge Exam. Eligible applicants are high school students in Oklahoma enrolled in the AOPA Foundation You Can Fly STEM curriculum.
FAA Private Pilot Knowledge Exam, FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Knowledge Exam, Aviation STEM Curriculum

rows.name: CAE 2025 Citation Bravo Type Rating Scholarship
values: CAE 2025 Citation Bravo Type Rating Scholarship

Awards a Pilot In Command (PIC) type rating for Cessna Citation Sovereign, Cessna Citation Bravo/Ultra, or Beechcraft King Air 350i. Applicants must hold a private pilot certificate (500 hours PIC) with multiengine (100 hours) and instrument (100 hours) ratings. The recipient will also serve as a CAE Women In Flight Ambassador.

rows.name: Dare to Dream Scholarship
values: Awards $4,000 to a WAI member who is working toward an instrument or multi-engine rating, commercial or CFI certificate. Funds are paid directly to the flight school and training must be completed within one year. Applicants must have a private pilot certificate and will be chosen based on merit, career aspirations, dedication, and community contributions.
Flight Training, Instrument Rating, Multi-Engine Rating, Commercial Certificate, CFI Certificate

rows.name: ISA+21 Airline Type Rating Scholarship
values: International Society of Women Airline Pilots (ISA+21)

Awards one type rating (B737 or A320) valued at $10,000 to a WAI member. The successful candidate will train for eight days with Flight Training International (FTI) in Miami, Florida, or Denver, Colorado. Training must be completed within 18 months, and finalists will be interviewed at the WAI2025 Conference.

rows.name: American Airlines Engineering Scholarship
values: Awards two $5,000 scholarships to students pursuing an engineering degree with a passion for the airline/aviation industry. Candidates are evaluated on academic standing, accomplishments, teamwork, leadership, and community service. Requirements include a 3.0 GPA or higher, enrollment in an accredited U.S. engineering program, and U.S. citizenship or permanent residency.

rows.name: Delta Air Lines Engineering Scholarship
values: Awards a $5,000 scholarship to a student currently enrolled in a baccalaureate degree in aerospace/aeronautical, electrical, or mechanical engineering. Includes a trip to the WAI2025 conference. Applicants must be full-time junior or senior level students with a cumulative 3.0 GPA or better.
Aerospace/Aeronautical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering

rows.name: The Al Worden “Endeavour” Scholarship
values: Offers an all-expenses-paid, 10-day journey to Washington, DC, and Space Camp at the U.S. Space & Rocket Center in Huntsville, Alabama, in July 2025 for STEM-minded students and teachers. Eight teams of four students and one teacher from specific countries will be selected. Applicants must submit a 3-minute video explaining what this opportunity and a future in STEM mean to them.

rows.name: The Carol M. SaNogueira Memorial Scholarship (Engineering)
values: The Carol M. SaNogueira Memorial Scholarship (Engineering)

Offers a $1,000 scholarship for engineering to women pursuing a career in the aerospace industry who reside, work, or go to school in Connecticut. Preference is given to Connecticut residents, but all applicants are considered based on character, need, and accomplishments. The award must be used for educational purposes at an accredited college or university.

rows.name: The NKL Aerospace Engineering Scholarship
values: Awards $1,000 to an applicant enrolled or accepted in an accredited two- or four-year college, technical institution, or certificate program with a declared major in aerospace engineering. Requires a minimum 3.0 GPA, U.S. citizenship or eligible noncitizen status, and volunteer experience in STEM/aviation. Applicants must submit a 500-1,000 word essay addressing financial need, inspiration, career path, and community involvement.

rows.name: Yukiko Howell Memorial Scholarship
values: Offers a $1,500 scholarship for STEM education in memory of Yukiko Howell. STEM careers include science, engineering, air traffic controller, avionics technician, dispatch certification, aircraft mechanic, meteorologist, and STEM educator.
STEM Education, Science, Engineering, Air Traffic Controller, Avionics Technician, Dispatch Certification, Aircraft Mechanic, Meteorologist, STEM Educator

rows.name: Alaska Airlines/Horizon Air Maintenance Scholarship
values: Awards one $5,000 scholarship to a female mechanic pursuing an A&P certification with the goal of working for Alaska Air Group. Applicants must be enrolled in an accredited aviation maintenance program or the Alaska Airlines Maintenance Technician Development program and be in good academic standing.

rows.name: Amazon Maintenance Technician Scholarship
values: Offers a $2,500 scholarship to a remarkable woman currently enrolled in an Aviation Maintenance Program (A&P) or an aspiring maintenance technician. Recognizes academic excellence, leadership potential, and dedication to the aviation community. Requires current WAI membership, a 500-word essay, and two letters of recommendation.

rows.name: American Airlines Aircraft Maintenance Technician Scholarship
values: American Airlines Aircraft Maintenance Technician Scholarship

Awards two $5,000 scholarships to students enrolled in an Aviation Maintenance Program (A&P) or pursuing a degree in aviation maintenance technology. Candidates are evaluated on academic standing, accomplishments, teamwork, leadership, and community service. Requirements include a 3.0 GPA or higher, enrollment in an accredited U.S. maintenance program, and U.S. citizenship or permanent residency.

rows.name: CAE 2025 Bombardier Learjet Maintenance Initial Scholarship
values: CAE 2025 Bombardier Learjet Maintenance Initial Scholarship

Awards one FAA maintenance initial scholarship for Bombardier Lear 60 or Lear 45. The course is 10 days in Dallas, Texas. The scholarship winner should have knowledge and experience for ICAO licenses or equivalent. The award must be started within one year of the scholarship award date. The recipient will also serve as a CAE Women In Flight Ambassador.

rows.name: Delta Air Lines Aircraft Maintenance Technology Scholarship
values: Delta Air Lines Aircraft Maintenance Technology Scholarship

Awards a $5,000 scholarship to a student enrolled in an Aviation Maintenance Technician Program (A&P) or pursuing a degree in Aviation Maintenance Technology. Includes a trip to the WAI2025 conference. Applicants must be full-time students with a cumulative 3.0 GPA or better and be a U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen.

rows.name: Epic Flight Academy Aircraft Mechanic Part 147 Scholarship
values: Epic Flight Academy Aircraft Mechanic Part 147 Scholarship

Awards one scholarship to a WAI member pursuing an aircraft maintenance license. Training takes place at Epic’s New Smyrna Beach, Florida, location. Applicants must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents, able to speak, read, write, and understand English, and at least 18 years old (or with parent/guardian approval if under 18). Training must start within 12 months of receiving the scholarship.

rows.name: Flexjet Aircraft Maintenance Scholarship
values: Awards one $2,000 scholarship to a student enrolled in an Aviation Maintenance Technician Program (A&P) or a degree in Aviation Maintenance Technology. Candidates are evaluated on academic standing, accomplishments, teamwork, leadership, and community service. Requirements include a 3.0 GPA or higher, enrollment in an accredited U.S. maintenance program, and U.S. citizenship or permanent residency. Includes a tour of Flexjet headquarters and a meet and greet.

rows.name: Pratt & Whitney Engine Maintenance Training Scholarship
values: Pratt & Whitney Engine Maintenance Training Scholarship

Offers six engine maintenance training scholarships to individuals working to become A&P mechanics. Includes one pre-scheduled Pratt & Whitney or Pratt & Whitney Canada engine maintenance training course, domestic airfare, and hotel accommodations. Scholarships expire two years from receipt. Applicants must be close to finishing AMT schooling and obtaining their A&P license, or be recent graduates.

rows.name: PSA Airlines Maintenance Scholarship
values: Provides a $3,000 scholarship to a WAI member pursuing a career in commercial aviation as an A&P mechanic. Candidates should display characteristics of being driven, reliable, and caring, with a passion for aviation.

rows.name: The Carol M. SaNogueira Memorial Scholarship (A&P)
values: The Carol M. SaNogueira Memorial Scholarship (A&P)

Offers a $500 scholarship for A&P to women pursuing a career in the aerospace industry who reside, work, or go to school in Connecticut. Preference is given to Connecticut residents, but all applicants are considered based on character, need, and accomplishments. The award must be used for educational purposes at an accredited college or university.

rows.name: Southwest Airlines Maintenance Scholarship
values: Presents two maintenance scholarships of $2,000 each. Each scholarship includes WAI conference admission, hotel accommodations, airfare (Southwest Airlines destination), and a small toolbox with the Southwest Airlines emblem.

rows.name: AeroStar ATP CTP Certification Training Scholarship
values: AeroStar ATP CTP Certification Training Scholarship

Covers the ATP CTP course, a prerequisite for the FAA’s highest certificate. This 7-9 day training program includes ground academics and flight simulation training. Successful completion makes the recipient eligible to take the ATP MultiEngine (ATM) knowledge test. Training must be scheduled to commence no later than one year from the award.

rows.name: Bonita Jean Olsen Memorial Scholarship
values: Awards $3,000 to an applicant pursuing higher education toward a STEM career with plans to enter aviation or aerospace. Must be enrolled (or committed) to an accredited institution (2-year, 4-year, technical, certificate) and have volunteered in STEM/aviation events. Preference for local candidates in Seattle/Washington state, but all considered based on character, need, involvement, and accomplishments.

rows.name: Business Aviation Collective Scheduler Course
values: Offers one Business Aviation Scheduler Course to a WAI member to help them pursue active employment as a Part 91 scheduler. The course must be used within one year of receiving the award. The recipient also receives access to the BAC Schedulers Resource Page.

rows.name: Elisha Hall Memorial Scholarship
values: Offers a $2,500 scholarship to a woman seeking to further her aviation career in flight training, aircraft scheduling/dispatch, aviation management, or aviation maintenance/avionics. Preference is given to local candidates in the Cincinnati, Ohio/Tri-State area, but all applicants are considered based on character, need, community involvement, and accomplishments. Limited financial assistance for WAI conference attendance is also offered.
Flight Training, Aircraft Scheduling, Dispatch, Aviation Management, Aviation Maintenance, Avionics

rows.name: General Chuck Yeager’s Legacy Foundation Scholarship
values: General Chuck Yeager’s Legacy Foundation Scholarship

Awards $1,000 to a deserving WAI member who shows tenacity and dedication by constructively overcoming obstacles in their aviation goals. Honors Brig. Gen. Charles “Chuck” Yeager. Additional essay questions are required for this application.

rows.name: Janet Clark Memorial Scholarship
values: Offers a $1,500 scholarship in memory of Janet Clark, an FAA airworthiness aviation safety inspector. Applicant must be working toward an aviation career, enrolled in an accredited aviation-related program, and have volunteered in WAI or aviation-related events. Requires detailed explanations of career plans, goals, and volunteer experiences.

rows.name: Level Up Aviation General Scholarship
values: Provides $1,000 for general career advancement in an aviation-related career (maintenance, ATC, scheduling, engineering, etc.) to economically disadvantaged and underrepresented groups. Applicants must be enrolled in a certification or degree program. Funds are paid directly to the training organization.
General Career Advancement, Aviation-Related Fields (Maintenance, ATC, Scheduling, Engineering)

rows.name: Mary Ann Eiff Memorial Outreach Award
values: Mary Ann Eiff Memorial Outreach Award

Recognizes an individual, WAI chapter, or entity demonstrating commitment to outreach activities for young women in aviation careers. Individual winners receive a lifetime WAI membership ($1,500 value); chapters receive a $1,500 contribution. Applicants must be current WAI members or active WAI chapters and submit a 500-word essay and two letters of recommendation.

rows.name: WASP Elaine D. Harmon Tailwheel Scholarship
values: WASP Elaine D. Harmon Tailwheel Scholarship

Provides up to $1,500 to fund tailwheel endorsement training, encouraging pilots to get involved in the warbird and vintage aircraft community. Intended for pilots interested in further training to fly warbirds or vintage planes. Applicants must be current WAI members and funds must be used within one year.

rows.name: Alaska Airlines / Horizon Air Pilot Scholarship
values: Alaska Airlines / Horizon Air Pilot Scholarship

Awards one $5,000 scholarship to a female pilot pursuing a professional airline pilot career with the goal of working for Alaska Air Group. Applicants must be full-time college students at the junior or senior level with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 or interested in their Pilot Development Program. Evaluated on volunteer work, academic standing, teamwork, leadership, and airmanship.

rows.name: American Airlines Flight Educational Scholarship
values: Awards up to four $5,000 educational scholarships to qualified WAI members. Funds can be used for flight training such as private pilot, instrument, multiengine, commercial, instructor, or ATP certificates. Applicants must have a high school diploma, be at least 18, and have enrolled in private pilot ground school or logged flight time. Requires addressing specific questions in the essay.
Flight Training (Private, Instrument, Multiengine, Commercial, Instructor, ATP)

rows.name: The Anne Bridge Baddour Aviation Scholarship
values: The Anne Bridge Baddour Aviation Scholarship

Awards $5,000 to a female U.S. citizen pilot dedicated to becoming a professional pilot. Must have at least a private pilot certificate with 150 hours of flying time and be on track toward earning the ATP. Award is for instrument rating, multi-engine rating, or ATP.
Professional Pilot, Instrument Rating, Multi-Engine Rating, ATP

rows.name: Delta Air Lines Propel Pilot Scholarship
values: Delta Air Lines Propel Pilot Scholarship

Awards two $5,000 scholarships to WAI members currently participating in Delta’s Propel Program (collegiate, company, or community partner path). Includes a trip to the WAI2025 conference. Intended for women seeking advancement in professional aviation development toward a career as a professional airline pilot.

rows.name: FedEx Flight Training Scholarship
values: Awards a $5,000 scholarship to a female WAI member pursuing her dream in aviation. Can be used toward an instrument or multiengine rating, commercial or CFI certificate. Funds are paid directly to the flight school and training must be completed within one year. Applicant must have a current private pilot certificate.
Flight Training, Instrument Rating, Multiengine Rating, Commercial Certificate, CFI Certificate

rows.name: Frontier Airlines Flight Training Scholarship
values: Awards a $5,000 scholarship for a female seeking a career as a professional airline pilot. Applicant must be a full-time junior, senior, or graduate student enrolled in an accredited collegiate aviation or aeronautical science program. Requires a minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA and FAA Instrument rating; Commercial Certificate and Multi-Engine Rating preferred. Funds paid to flight school, training completed within one year.

rows.name: ISA+21 Financial Scholarship 2025
values: International Society of Women Airline Pilots (ISA+21)

Awards a minimum of two $5,000 scholarships to women working to acquire a CFI, CFII, or MEI certificate. Funds are paid directly to an accredited college/university with an aviation curriculum, an aviation technical school, or a government-approved flight school. Training must be completed within one year of the award.

rows.name: PSA Airlines Flight Scholarship
values: Provides a $3,000 scholarship to a WAI member pursuing a career in commercial aviation as a professional pilot. Candidates must hold a private pilot license and display characteristics of being driven, reliable, and caring, with a passion for aviation.

rows.name: Republic Airways Opportunity Elevated Scholarship
values: Awards a $5,000 scholarship to a female commercial pilot pursuing a professional pilot career. Candidates are evaluated on academic standing, accomplishments, teamwork, leadership skills, and airmanship. Applicants must be RJet Cadets with Republic Airways.

rows.name: Russ Cotney and Lauren Cotney Professional Airline Pilot Career Scholarship
values: Russ Cotney and Lauren Cotney Professional Airline Pilot Career Scholarship

Awards $2,500 to women pursuing a professional airline pilot career as a junior, senior, or graduate-level student in an accredited college or university aviation, engineering, or aeronautical science program. Preference for veterans, current service members, or daughters of veterans/service members. Requires minimum 3.0 GPA, two letters of recommendation, and an essay detailing goals, achievements, and community involvement.
Professional Airline Pilot, Aviation, Engineering, Aeronautical Science

rows.name: Sun Country Airlines “Fly in a New Direction” Scholarship
values: Sun Country Airlines “Fly in a New Direction” Scholarship

Awards a $5,000 scholarship to a female applicant passionate about becoming a career pilot. Applicants must be pursuing a professional career pilot path, hold a private pilot certificate, and be pursuing an advanced pilot certificate or rating. Funds are paid directly to the flight school and must be used within a year.

rows.name: WAI | United Aviate Academy Full Flight Training Scholarship
values: WAI, United Aviate Academy, Chase Bank
WAI | United Aviate Academy Full Flight Training Scholarship

Awards two full scholarships, valued at $88,600 each, to students currently enrolled and progressing through the United Aviate Academy program. Aims to promote diversity and inclusion by reducing the cost barrier for individuals aspiring to commercial airline pilot careers. Finalists will have a video interview.

rows.name: WAI | United Aviate Academy Partial Scholarship
values: FOUR OFFERED – TWO each at $11,000 value and TWO each at $12,000 value
WAI, United Aviate Academy, Chase Bank
WAI | United Aviate Academy Partial Scholarship

Awards a total of four partial scholarships (two at $12,000 each and two at $11,000 each) to students currently enrolled and progressing through the United Aviate Academy program. Funds cover tuition and fees related to attendance. Aims to promote diversity and inclusion by reducing the cost barrier for individuals aspiring to commercial airline pilot careers. Finalists will have a video interview.

rows.name: ADF/North American Flight Control Dispatch Certificate Scholarship
values: Airline Dispatchers Federation, North American Flight Control LLC
ADF/North American Flight Control Dispatch Certificate Scholarship

Offers a scholarship to WAI members to earn their Aircraft Dispatcher’s FAA 121 certificate. Covers tuition, books, instruction, and training for the written test and checkride, including FAA examiner’s fees. Recipient is responsible for travel, lodging, and meals. Training must be completed with North American Flight Control prior to December 31, 2025.

rows.name: Southwest Airlines Dispatch Certification Scholarship
values: Awards an aircraft dispatcher certificate to a WAI member aspiring to become an aircraft dispatcher. No previous aviation experience required. Applicant must be able to read, write, speak, and understand English, have a high school diploma or GED, and be at least 21 years old. Funds are paid directly to the dispatch school.

rows.name: Universal Weather & Aviation FAA-Certified Dispatcher Training Course Scholarship
values: Universal Weather & Aviation FAA-Certified Dispatcher Training Course Scholarship

Offers a hybrid aircraft dispatcher course scholarship, consisting of a self-paced online portion and an eight-day classroom session in Houston, Texas. The online coursework can be completed over four to eight months. After meeting online requirements and passing the FAA Airman Knowledge Test, the recipient completes the practical portion at the Houston facility.

rows.name: Level Up Aviation Helo Scholarship
values: Provides $1,000 to an individual pursuing their private or commercial helicopter rating. Applicants must be enrolled in an FAA-approved Part 141 or international equivalent program and expect to receive their commercial helicopter pilot rating after March 1, 2026.

rows.name: Amazon.com, Professional Flight Training Scholarship
values: Offers a $2,500 scholarship to a remarkable woman enrolled in flight training. Recognizes academic excellence, leadership potential, and dedication to the aviation community. Requires current WAI membership, a 500-word essay, and two letters of recommendation.

rows.name: Bunny M. Connors Memorial Scholarship
values: Awards $979.82 to a WAI member pursuing a private pilot certificate or instrument rating. Flight training must be completed within one year of receiving the scholarship. Honors Bunny M. Connors, a respiratory therapist who pursued her dream of flying and became a flight instructor and commercial airline pilot.
Private Pilot Certificate, Instrument Rating, Flight Training

rows.name: Delta Air Lines Pilot Scholarship
values: Awards a $5,000 scholarship to a WAI member working toward instrument, commercial, CFI, CFII, MEI, and primary certificates. Includes a trip to the WAI2025 conference. Funds are paid directly to the flight school, and training must be completed within a year. Intended for women seeking advancement in professional aviation development toward a professional airline pilot career.
Pilot Certificates (Instrument, Commercial, CFI, CFII, MEI, Primary), Professional Airline Pilot

rows.name: Christine Reed Memorial Flight Scholarship
values: Women in Aviation International (WAI) in partnership with J. Elliot Marketing

Offers a $2,500 flight training scholarship in memory of Christine Reed. Open to women ages 16-30 who have soloed within the last six months and are working toward recreational, sport pilot, or private pilot certificates (advanced certificates/ratings may be considered). Applicants must provide a copy of their solo endorsement. Preference for New Jersey, Illinois, and Arizona residents.
Flight Training (Recreational, Sport Pilot, Private Pilot, Advanced Certificates/Ratings)

rows.name: Diane Ballweg Scholarship
values: Awards $500 to a woman over 30 years old who wants to learn to fly or who already has a private, sport, or recreational certificate and wants to pursue an advanced certificate or rating (instrument, commercial, or other). The scholarship award will be paid directly to the flight school.
Flight Training (Private, Sport, Recreational, Instrument, Commercial, Advanced Ratings)

rows.name: Esther Noffke Flight Training Scholarship
values: Awards one $5,000 flight training scholarship in memory of aviation pioneer Esther Noffke. Applicants must be enrolled in a flight program or college/university, maintain a 3.0 GPA or higher, and provide at least one reference letter. It is needs-based, requiring applicants to outline their financial situation in an essay. Award winner will meet quarterly with an assigned mentor.

rows.name: ISA+21 Francesca Norris Memorial Scholarship
values: International Society of Women Airline Pilots (ISA+21), Francesca Norris Memorial Fund, U.S. Aviation Academy

Awards two $5,000 scholarships to women working to acquire a CFI, CFII, or MEI rating, in honor of Francesca Norris. Recipients will attend the U.S. Aviation Academy in Denton, Texas, for their training. One scholarship is co-sponsored by the U.S. Aviation Academy.

rows.name: Kelsey A. Meyer Memorial Scholarship
values: Awards one $2,500 scholarship annually to a female college sophomore or above student enrolled in an aviation/professional flight degree program at an accredited university. Requires a minimum GPA of 3.0. Funds must be used for educational and flight-related expenses and within one year of receiving the award.

rows.name: Kylie Murray Memorial Women in Aviation International Scholarship
values: Kylie Murray Memorial Women in Aviation International Scholarship

Awards one $7,500 scholarship for flight training for commercial multiengine land (C-MEL) or certified flight instructor—multiengine (MEI) certification, in partnership with ATP Flight School. Recipient must meet requirements including WAI membership, U.S. citizenship/permanent residency, current FAA medical certificate, commercial pilot certificate with instrument rating, and student-athlete activity. Travel, lodging, or examiner’s fees are not included.
Commercial Multiengine Land (C-MEL), Certified Flight Instructor—Multiengine (MEI)

rows.name: Martha King Scholarship for Female Flight Instructors
values: Martha King Scholarship for Female Flight Instructors

Awards a scholarship to a female pilot working on an initial flight instructor certificate or a new rating on her flight instructor certificate. Includes $5,000, lifetime access to King Schools online courses (valued at $13,120), and FIRCs for life. Applicant must be a WAI member holding a current FAA commercial certificate with an instrument rating, or a CFI certificate. Essay should include aviation history, goals, and financial need.
Flight Instructor Certificate (Initial CFI, CFI Add-on Rating)

rows.name: MzeroA Gold Lifetime Membership Scholarship
values: Awards a Gold Lifetime Membership to the MzeroA Online Ground School, valued at $2,497. Provides access to full private, instrument, commercial, certified flight instructor, and fundamentals of instruction ground schools, over 320 HD training videos, live weekly workshops, Q&A sessions, mock checkrides, and a member-only forum.
Flight Training, Ground School (Private, Instrument, Commercial, CFI, FOI)

rows.name: The Carol M. SaNogueira Memorial Scholarship (Pilot)
values: The Carol M. SaNogueira Memorial Scholarship (Pilot)

Offers a $500 scholarship for pilot training to women pursuing a career in the aerospace industry who reside, work, or go to school in Connecticut. Preference is given to Connecticut residents, but all applicants are considered based on character, need, and accomplishments. The award must be used for educational purposes at an accredited college or university.

rows.name: Sporty’s Foundation Flight Training Scholarship for WAI Chapter Member
values: Sporty’s Foundation Flight Training Scholarship for WAI Chapter Member

Offers one $5,000 flight training scholarship to a WAI member who works with youth to help them pursue aviation dreams and is pursuing a recreational, sport, or private pilot certificate. Special consideration for Girls in Aviation Day volunteers. Funds are for flight training costs only, must be used within one year, and are sent to the recipient’s flight school. Includes Sporty’s complete Learn to Fly Flight Training Course.
Flight Training (Recreational, Sport, Private Pilot Certificate)

rows.name: The Dorothy Thompson/Tampa Bay Aviation Scholarship
values: The Dorothy Thompson/Tampa Bay Aviation Scholarship

Offers one $1,500 scholarship to a WAI member pursuing a fixed-wing or rotorcraft, private or commercial pilot certificate, or instrument rating. The scholarship is a credit on their account at Tampa Bay Aviation. Funds cannot be disbursed directly to the recipient and must be used for a certificate or rating, not just aircraft rental.
Fixed-wing/Rotorcraft Pilot Certificate (Private, Commercial), Instrument Rating

rows.name: The Keep Flying International Scholarship
values: Offers two $3,000 scholarships to WAI members worldwide for intermediate level flight training. For individuals working on a fixed-wing aircraft instrument, commercial, multi-engine, or flight instructor certificate. Candidates must hold a private pilot certificate, have at least 100 hours of flight time, and have passed all written exams for the sought certificate. Finalists will be interviewed.
Fixed-wing Aircraft Instrument, Commercial, Multi-engine, Flight Instructor Certificate

rows.name: The White Family Legacy Scholarship
values: Offers one $3,000 scholarship to an individual working on a fixed-wing aircraft instrument or multiengine rating, or commercial or CFI certificate. Funds are paid directly to the flight school, and training must be completed within one year. Minimum requirements include a private pilot certificate, 100 hours of flight time, and current written test results. Selection based on merit, career aspirations, dedication, and community contributions.
Fixed-wing Aircraft Instrument/Multiengine Rating, Commercial/CFI Certificate

rows.name: WAI Atlanta “Wheels Down South” Chapter Scholarship
values: WAI Atlanta “Wheels Down South” Chapter Scholarship

Offers a $1,000 scholarship to aid an individual with their aviation dream (flight, maintenance, management, etc.). Applicants are evaluated based on merit, career aspirations, dedication, community contributions, and following application directions. Preference for Atlanta Chapter members. Funds must be used within one year of acceptance and are paid directly to the organization.

rows.name: Wings for Val Foundation Lieutenant Valerie Cappelaere Delaney Memorial Scholarship
values: Wings for Val Foundation Lieutenant Valerie Cappelaere Delaney Memorial Scholarship

Honors Lt. Valerie “Val” Delaney and supports women in aviation. Open to female WAI members from any country, 18 years or older, pursuing a private fixed-wing pilot certificate or any subsequent flight ratings. Applicants are encouraged to research Val and draw similarities in their essay. FAA Class 1-3 medicals preferred; Basic Medical considered. Funds paid directly to flight school and must be used within one year.
Private Fixed-wing Pilot Certificate, Flight Ratings

rows.name: Wings Over 35 Scholarship
values: Designed to promote general aviation among men or women over the age of 35 to attain private pilot certification. Applicant must be over 35, not hold a private pilot certificate, desire higher ratings, and hold at least an FAA Class 3 medical. Essay should explain aviation goals, progress, and general financial need. Funds paid directly to flight school and must be used within one year.

rows.name: The LeRoy W. Homer Jr. Foundation Scholarship
values: The LeRoy W. Homer Jr. Foundation, P.O. Box 268, Marlton, NJ 08053
The LeRoy W. Homer Jr. Foundation Scholarship

The LeRoy W. Homer Jr. Foundation Scholarship empowers future aviators to pursue their dreams of flight. Applicants must submit a completed application, including two letters of recommendation, by the annual January 31st deadline. Essays should detail the applicant's inspiration to become a pilot and must be original content.

rows.name: FOR LOVE OF COUNTRY SCHOLARSHIP
values: Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum (PHAM) Educational Endowment, Rick & Teresa Price Family

The Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum (PHAM) Educational Endowment funds educational efforts and awards scholarships for individuals committed to a career in aviation. This scholarship supports future aviation students, with over $190,000 awarded to date. A matching gift challenge is in place to strengthen the endowment and provide immediate scholarships.

rows.name: ADMIRAL RONALD J. HAYS SCHOLARSHIP
values: This scholarship is offered by the Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum to support students, with a variable award amount.

rows.name: BRIG GEN ROBERT B. AND JUDITH MAGUIRE SCHOLARSHIP
values: BRIG GEN ROBERT B. AND JUDITH MAGUIRE SCHOLARSHIP
This scholarship is offered by the Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum to support students, with a variable award amount.

rows.name: COL. ROBERT P. MOORE SCHOLARSHIP - INITIAL PILOT TRAINING
values: COL. ROBERT P. MOORE SCHOLARSHIP - INITIAL PILOT TRAINING
This scholarship, offered by the Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum, supports individuals pursuing initial pilot training, with a variable award amount.

rows.name: COL. ROBERT P. MOORE SCHOLARSHIP - FAA CERTIFIED FLIGHT INSTRUCTOR (CFI)
values: COL. ROBERT P. MOORE SCHOLARSHIP - FAA CERTIFIED FLIGHT INSTRUCTOR (CFI)
This scholarship, offered by the Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum, supports individuals pursuing FAA Certified Flight Instructor (CFI) training, with a variable award amount.

rows.name: FRANK DER YUEN AVIATION SCHOLARSHIP
values: This aviation scholarship is offered by the Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum to support students, with a variable award amount.

rows.name: AVIATION PATHWAYS GRANTS
values: Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum, Ray Foundation

The Aviation Pathways Grant provides financial support of up to $10,000 to Hawaii youth (ages 16-21) to help them achieve their private pilot’s license (PPL). Recipients, called Pathfinders, receive educational and programmatic support, including flight simulator training, ground school, and mentorship, to prepare for aviation careers.

rows.name: COL. ROBERT F. SZUL SCHOLARSHIP
values: This scholarship is offered by the Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum to support students, with a variable award amount.

rows.name: PETER STARN YOUTH EDUCATIONAL ENDOWMENT
values: This educational endowment is offered by the Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum to support youth, with a variable award amount.

rows.name: STATE UNIVERSITY SCHOLARSHIPS
values: This entry refers to a list of scholarships previously applied to by WHS students at a State University. It serves as a reference guide for past research efforts, and applicants need to validate current status and dates through provided links.

rows.name: FVCC SCHOLARSHIPS
values: This is a reference guide for scholarships previously applied to by WHS students through FVCC. Applicants need to validate the current status and dates through the provided links.

rows.name: MILITARY Scholarships
values: Mentors through past searches with WHS students

This entry serves as a reference guide for military-focused scholarships previously identified by mentors for WHS students. It is not actively maintained for current dates or renewal information. Applicants are advised to validate the current status and application details through external links.

rows.name: All Other Scholarships
values: Mentors through past searches with other WHS students
This entry serves as a reference guide for scholarships previously identified and applied to by WHS students through mentor searches.

rows.name: Fly for Duke Aviation Scholarship
values: This scholarship provides financial assistance and mentoring to aspiring aviators aged 17-24 to earn a private pilot's license. Applicants must be U.S. citizens and train at an FAA-approved flight school, completing ground school and obtaining a 3rd class medical prior to flight training. The scholarship aims to help recipients achieve their aviation goals in honor of Duke Carrillo's dream.

rows.name: Richard L. Taylor Flight Training Scholarship
values: Richard L. Taylor Flight Training Scholarship

This scholarship is for college or university students continuing their education in the aviation industry, specifically enrolled in a flight program with aspirations to become a professional pilot. Applicants must have a private pilot's license and a GPA of 3.0 or greater. High school seniors planning a career in general aviation are also eligible.

rows.name: Gene Baker Memorial Scholarship
values: Open to AEA members, their children, grandchildren, or dependents. This scholarship can be used for any field of study at an accredited college or university and is applied toward tuition only. Applicants must be at least a high school senior or graduate and plan to pursue a degree at an accredited U.S. post-secondary institution or international equivalent.

rows.name: Jim Cook Honorary Scholarship
values: Open to AEA members, their children, grandchildren, or dependents. This scholarship can be used for any field of study at an accredited college or university and is applied toward tuition only. Applicants must be at least a high school senior or graduate and plan to pursue a degree at an accredited U.S. post-secondary institution or international equivalent.

rows.name: Monte Mitchell Scholarship
values: This annual scholarship honors Monte Mitchell's service to the Aircraft Electronics Association and general aviation industry. It is awarded to an AEA member employee for exemplary job performance and pursuit of professional development. The scholarship covers full AEA Convention registration, travel, and hotel expenses.

rows.name: Chuck Freeland Memorial Scholarship for Flight Training
values: Chuck Freeland Memorial Scholarship for Flight Training

Named in memory of Chuck Freeland, this scholarship is available to employees of AEA member companies who plan to pursue a recreational or private pilot certificate. The award money is to be used for flight training costs only and the recipient must plan to pursue a Private Pilot Certificate within six months of receiving the scholarship.

rows.name: Sporty's Foundation Private Pilot Training for AEA Technicians
values: Sporty's Foundation Private Pilot Training for AEA Technicians

Sponsored by The Sporty's Foundation, this scholarship is available to avionics technicians or avionics managers of an AEA Repair Station Member. It is intended to be used toward achieving their Private Pilot Certificate.

rows.name: Aircraft Lighting International Scholarship
values: Available to a high school senior or college student who plans to attend or is attending an accredited school in an avionics or aircraft maintenance program.

rows.name: James Hammond Joubert Memorial Scholarship
values: Named in memory of Jim Joubert, founder of Pacific Southwest Instruments, this scholarship is available to a high school senior or college student who plans to attend or is attending an accredited school in an avionics or aircraft maintenance program.

rows.name: Pat Napolitano Memorial Scholarship for Aspiring Technicians
values: Pat Napolitano Memorial Scholarship for Aspiring Technicians

This scholarship honors Pat Napolitano's legacy and is available to all graduating seniors or current college students pursuing their Aviation Technician Certification. It aims to inspire a new generation of aviators.
Aviation Technician Certification, Aircraft Maintenance, Avionics

rows.name: Chuck Peacock Memorial Scholarship
values: Given by Wanda Peacock in memory of her late husband, Chuck Peacock, founder of the Aircraft Electronics Association. This scholarship recognizes the importance of management skills and is available to a high school senior or college student who plans to attend or is attending an accredited school in an aviation management program.

rows.name: David Arver Memorial Scholarship
values: Given by Dutch and Ginger Arver in memory of their son, David. The recipient of this scholarship shall be a high school senior or college student who plans to attend or is attending an accredited school in an avionics or aircraft maintenance program.

rows.name: Dutch and Ginger Arver Scholarship
values: Available to a high school senior or college student who plans to attend or is attending an accredited school in an avionics or aircraft maintenance program.

rows.name: Garmin Scholarship
values: Available to a high school senior or college student who plans to attend or is attending an accredited school in an avionics or aircraft maintenance program.

rows.name: Garmin–Jerry Smith Memorial Scholarship
values: Available to a high school, college or vocational/technical school student who plans to attend or is attending an accredited school in an avionics or aircraft maintenance program.

rows.name: Gogo Scholarship
values: Established through a donation from Gogo, this $2,500 annual scholarship is presented each year to a high school senior and/or college student. It is for those who plan to attend or are attending an accredited school in an avionics or aircraft maintenance program.

rows.name: Johnny Davis Memorial Scholarship
values: Named in memory of Johnny Davis, president of Dallas Avionics, this scholarship is available to a high school senior or college student. It is for those who plan to attend or are attending an accredited school in an avionics or aircraft maintenance program.

rows.name: Kevin Miesbach Memorial Scholarship
values: This scholarship celebrates Kevin Miesbach's contribution to the avionics technician field and shares his passion for the value of a career as an avionics technician. It is available to a high school senior or college student who plans to attend or is attending an accredited school in an avionics or aircraft maintenance program.

rows.name: Lee Tarbox Memorial Scholarship
values: Given by Pacific Southwest Instruments, this scholarship is available to a high school senior or college student who plans to attend or is attending an accredited school in an avionics or aircraft maintenance program.

rows.name: Marshall Temple Memorial Scholarship
values: Named in memory of Marshall E. Temple, founder of Temple Electronics, this scholarship is available to a high school senior or college student. It is for those who plan to attend or is attending an accredited school in an avionics or aircraft maintenance program.

rows.name: Mid-Continent Instruments and Avionics Scholarship
values: Available to a high school senior or college student who plans to attend or is attending an accredited school in an avionics or aircraft maintenance program.

rows.name: Susan T. Friedle Scholarship
values: Available to a high school senior or college student who plans to attend or is attending an accredited school in an avionics or aircraft maintenance program.

rows.name: Universal Avionics Scholarship
values: Available to high school seniors and/or college students who plan to or are attending an accredited school in an avionics program or aircraft maintenance program.

rows.name: National Aviation Explorer Scholarship
values: National Aviation Exploring Committee / Learning for Life Corporation

The National Aviation Explorer Scholarship recognizes excellence among Aviation Explorers studying aviation technologies and skills. It encourages participants to pursue and complete an aviation curriculum, supporting future leadership in the field. Applicants must be active in an Aviation Explorer post and provide recommendation letters.

rows.name: Navigate Your Future Scholarship
values: The Navigate Your Future Scholarship is for high school graduates pursuing careers in general aviation. Applicants must be seniors in high school, accepted into an aviation-related program at an accredited college or university, and demonstrate an interest in general aviation. The scholarship provides $2,500 for one year of undergraduate study.

rows.name: Calvin L. Carrithers Aviation Scholarship 2026
values: This scholarship provides $1,000 annually to four American students dedicated to blogging weekly about flight training, flying, school, and their interest in aviation. Applicants must be U.S. citizens enrolled in a fully accredited university aviation program within the United States and be willing to write weekly blog posts.
Aviation (Commercial Aviation, Professional Pilot, Aviation Management, Airport Management)

rows.name: Sheltair & Avfuel: Future Takes Flight Scholarship Program
values: Sheltair & Avfuel: Future Takes Flight Scholarship Program

Sheltair and Avfuel provide six $5,000 scholarships annually across three categories: learning to fly or advanced pilot ratings, aviation technicians, and continuing education. The program aims to support career advancement opportunities within business aviation, with special consideration for financial hardship.

rows.name: AVTRIP Scholarship
values: The AVTRIP Scholarship awards one current AVTRIP member $2,000 to further their aviation education. Funds can be used for flight training, educational tuition fees, or a new license or rating.

rows.name: Avfuel Pilot-in-Training Scholarship
values: The Avfuel Pilot-in-Training Scholarship awards three students with funds ($1,500, $1,000, $500) to further their aviation education. Funds can be used for flight training, educational tuition fees, or a new license.

rows.name: Captain Judy Rice Pilot Scholarship for Flight Training
values: Captain Judy Rice Pilot Scholarship for Flight Training

This scholarship is for U.S. high school juniors or seniors interested in flight training at Epic Flight Academy. Applicants must be U.S. Citizens or Permanent Residents, 16 or older by December 31, 2026, and demonstrate exemplary dedication.

rows.name: Epic Pilot Scholarships for Flight Training
values: Epic Pilot Scholarships for Flight Training

These scholarships are for U.S. high school juniors or seniors interested in flight training at Epic Flight Academy. Applicants must be U.S. Citizens or Permanent Residents, 16 or older by December 31, 2026, and meet other general requirements.

rows.name: Epic Aircraft Mechanic Scholarship ($20,000)
values: These scholarships are for U.S. high school seniors interested in aircraft mechanic training at Epic Flight Academy. Applicants must be U.S. Citizens or Permanent Residents, 18 or older by the time of program completion, and meet other general requirements.

rows.name: Epic Aircraft Mechanic Scholarship ($10,000)
values: These scholarships are for U.S. high school seniors interested in aircraft mechanic training at Epic Flight Academy. Applicants must be U.S. Citizens or Permanent Residents, 18 or older by the time of program completion, and meet other general requirements.

rows.name: Strategic Partner Scholarships
values: Varies by chapter, winners announced May of following year
WTS Foundation / HNTB, AECOM, HDR, Jacobs, and WSP

These scholarships are sponsored by WTS International Pinnacle and Strategic Level Corporate Partners to support the development of students in the transportation field. They encourage bright new professionals and students to undertake careers in transportation.

rows.name: Sharon D. Banks Memorial Undergraduate Scholarship
values: Varies by chapter, winners announced May of following year
Sharon D. Banks Memorial Undergraduate Scholarship

This scholarship is awarded to women pursuing undergraduate studies in transportation or a related field. It honors Sharon D. Banks, a former general manager of Alameda-Contra Costa Transit District, who led efforts to motivate the public transit workforce.

rows.name: Helene M. Overly Memorial Graduate Scholarship
values: Varies by chapter, winners announced May of following year
Helene M. Overly Memorial Graduate Scholarship

Established in 1981, this scholarship honors Helene M. Overly for her dedicated service to WTS. Applicants must be enrolled in a graduate degree program in a transportation-related field such as engineering, planning, finance, or logistics.

rows.name: Molitoris Leadership Scholarship for Undergraduates
values: Varies by chapter, winners announced May of following year

This scholarship motivates and rewards women who demonstrate leadership in the transportation industry, ensuring that the essential leadership skills and perspectives of women are included in planning future transportation systems.

rows.name: Bridgette Beato Leadership Legacy Scholarship for Graduates
values: Varies by chapter, winners announced May of following year
Bridgette Beato Leadership Legacy Scholarship for Graduates

This scholarship honors past, present, and future WTS leaders by awarding an annual scholarship to female graduate students pursuing a career in transportation. Eligible candidates demonstrate leadership skills and an active commitment to community service, with an interest in sustainability, land use, environmental impact, security, and quality of life issues.
Transportation or a related field, with interest in sustainability, land use, environmental impact, security, and quality of life issues

rows.name: Junior College/Trade School Scholarship
values: Varies by chapter, winners announced May of following year

This scholarship fosters the development of women in the transportation field by encouraging bright new professionals to undertake careers in transportation. It is awarded to women pursuing transportation-related study at community, technical, or trade colleges, intended for students pursuing an Associate or technical degree.

rows.name: WTS Transportation YOU High School Scholarship
values: Varies by chapter, winners announced May of following year
WTS Transportation YOU High School Scholarship

WTS awards this scholarship to girls pursuing high school studies in science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM). It aims to foster the development of women and girls in the transportation field by encouraging bright new professionals and students to undertake careers in transportation.
Science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) related to transportation

rows.name: Print and Graphics Scholarship Foundation
values: The Print and Graphics Scholarship Foundation (PGSF) offers scholarships to undergraduate and technical school students pursuing careers in graphic communication. Eligible students must maintain a minimum 3.0 GPA and be enrolled in a printing or graphics program at an accredited institution. Awards vary from $1,000 to $5,000 per academic year and are renewable for up to four years.
Graphic Communication, Printing Technology, Printing Management, Packaging, Publishing

rows.name: Kitchen Cabinet Kings Entrepreneur Scholarship
values: The Kitchen Cabinet Kings Entrepreneur Scholarship supports young entrepreneurs pursuing higher education. Applicants must be U.S. citizens enrolled or planning to enroll in an accredited U.S. college, university, or trade school program.

rows.name: Surety Bond Authority Scholarship Program 2025
values: Surety Bond Authority Inc., 21300 Victory Blvd., Suite 300, Woodland Hills, CA 91367

This scholarship provides financial assistance to exceptional high school and college undergraduate students. Applicants must submit a 500- to 1,000-word essay detailing their choice to pursue a career in Accounting, Banking, Finance, or a related business field. The program aims to empower youth to achieve their academic aspirations and contribute to their communities.
Accounting, Banking, Finance, or a related business field

rows.name: Nelson Scholarship
values: The Nelson Scholarship awards $1,500 to students pursuing business, interior design, or architecture. Eligible applicants must be legal residents of the United States, enrolled in an accredited high school (senior year) or college/university (for at least one full calendar year). Funds can be used for educational expenses including tuition, books, and campus housing.

rows.name: Conquering Cancer Scholarship
values: The Conquering Cancer Scholarship is open to students who are currently fighting or have previously fought a cancer diagnosis, or have an immediate family member who has. Applicants must be enrolled or planning to enroll in an undergraduate or graduate program within the United States for the Spring 2026 semester. The scholarship aims to support students pursuing post-secondary education.

rows.name: Ted & Holly Rollins Scholarship
values: The Ted & Holly Rollins Scholarship offers $10,000 to high school seniors nationwide. Applicants must submit a 500-word essay detailing their life story, intended field of study, career aspirations, and how they plan to impact the world. The scholarship aims to support deserving students who demonstrate dedication and sweat equity to excel academically and in life.

rows.name: 2024 Lanford Family Transportation Construction Worker Memorial Scholarship Program
values: American Road & Transportation Builders Association Transportation Development Foundation (ARTBA-TDF)
2024 Lanford Family Transportation Construction Worker Memorial Scholarship Program

This scholarship provides financial assistance to help the sons, daughters, or legally adopted children of transportation construction industry workers killed or permanently disabled in the line of duty pursue post-high school education. Eligibility is limited to children whose parent was employed by a transportation construction firm or public agency at the time of their death or disabling injury in a roadway work zone accident.

rows.name: Obama-Chesky Voyager Scholarship for Public Service
values: Obama-Chesky Voyager Scholarship for Public Service

The Voyager Scholarship supports college sophomores passionate about public service and community impact. It provides up to $50,000 in financial aid for junior and senior years, a $10,000 stipend for a summer work-travel experience, and access to a network of leaders. Applicants must demonstrate financial need, a minimum 3.0 GPA, and a commitment to public service.

rows.name: 4-H Youth in Action Scholarship
values: The 4-H Youth in Action program recognizes 4-H members aged 14-19 who have made significant community contributions. Four award winners receive a $5,000 scholarship for higher education, professional development, and opportunities to serve as national youth representatives. Applicants need to demonstrate leadership, community impact, and a strong personal story of 4-H involvement.

rows.name: Davis-Putter Scholarship
values: The Davis-Putter Scholarship Fund provides financial support to students actively involved in progressive movements for liberation, self-determination, and social and economic justice. Awards are up to $15,000 per recipient annually and are renewable with reapplication. Applicants must demonstrate financial need and be enrolled in a degree, trade, or training program.
Progressive movements for liberation, self-determination and social and economic justice

rows.name: Next for Autism Fellows Scholarship
values: The NEXT for AUTISM Fellows Scholarship provides tuition assistance for undergraduate and graduate students studying Health and Human Services. Priority is given to those committed to serving individuals with autism post-graduation. It includes mentorship and requires enrollment in a NEXT for AUTISM partner school, while also paying participants to work as Direct Support Professionals.

rows.name: IMEG Engineering Scholarship
values: The IMEG Engineering Scholarship awards up to $10,000 to underrepresented college sophomores, juniors, and seniors pursuing engineering degrees. Applicants must be U.S. citizens, demonstrate financial need, and be full-time students in specified engineering and technology fields. The scholarship aims to support the next generation of innovators in engineering.

rows.name: Next Swell Scholarship
values: The Next Swell Scholarship provides $5,000 to exceptional graduate students pursuing research or a degree in marine science or marine conservation. Scholarships are merit-based and funds must be used for tuition, fees, or required course materials. Applicants must be U.S. citizens or Legal Permanent Residents with a minimum graduate GPA of 3.5.

rows.name: Catching The Dream Scholarship
values: The Catching The Dream Scholarship supports Native American college students demonstrating academic achievement, leadership, and a desire to help their communities. It offers awards ranging from $500 to $5,000 per year across three programs: MESBEC, NALE, and TBM. Applicants must be enrolled members with at least ", " degree American Indian blood from a federally recognized, state-recognized, or terminated U.S. Tribe.

rows.name: RMA Foundation Scholarship
values: The RMA Foundation Scholarship supports undergraduate students interested in a career in the financial industry, particularly banking. Awards range from $1,000 to $5,000 and are renewable for up to two additional years. Eligibility requires current undergraduate enrollment, demonstrated interest in banking through coursework or experience, and academic achievement.

rows.name: HITEC Foundation Scholarship
values: The HITEC Foundation Scholarship assists students of Hispanic descent pursuing a university degree in the technology industry. It offers up to $5,000 for accredited U.S. colleges, universities, or vocational/technical schools. Applicants must have Hispanic heritage, a minimum 3.0 GPA, and be a high school senior, current college student, graduate student, or DACA recipient majoring in a technology-related field.
This scholarship is for students pursuing studies in construction. It is part of a reference list of past scholarships applied to by WHS students.

rows.name: GRANGER MACDONALD / DOUG WISTNER SCHOLARSHIP
values: Applicant must be pursuing a degree or certificate in residential construction management or trades. Must have at least a 3.0 GPA and attend an accredited 4-year college or vo/tech school. Preference is given to Texas residents or students attending Texas schools.
Residential Construction Management, Residential Construction Trades

rows.name: HERMAN J. SMITH SCHOLARSHIP
values: Applicant must be pursuing a degree in residential construction management, mortgage finance, or a construction related field at an accredited 4-year institution. Must be a full-time undergraduate or graduate student with at least one full academic year remaining. High school seniors are not eligible.
Residential Construction Management, Mortgage Finance, Construction Related Field

rows.name: LEE S. EVANS SCHOLARSHIP
values: Applicant must be interested in a leadership role in the residential construction industry upon graduation. Must have at least one semester of completed college coursework and be enrolled full-time as an undergraduate or graduate student with one full academic year remaining. High school seniors and fifth-year undergraduates are not eligible.
Residential Construction Industry (leadership roles), Construction Management

rows.name: NATIONAL HOUSING ENDOWMENT EOC STUDENT SCHOLARSHIP FUND
values: NATIONAL HOUSING ENDOWMENT EOC STUDENT SCHOLARSHIP FUND

Applicant must be a child of a full- or part-time paid Executive Officer with a minimum of three years’ cumulative service for an NAHB affiliated association. Must be a graduating high school senior or have a diploma/GED, and be enrolled or accepted into an accredited two-year, four-year, or vo-tech school with full-time status. A minimum GPA of 2.5 is required.

rows.name: ROGER GLUNT/HELP STUDENT SCHOLARSHIP FUND
values: This scholarship is for undergraduate and graduate students enrolled in a construction management program receiving Homebuilding Education Leadership Program (HELP) funding in the current calendar year. Awards are based on academic transcript, residential construction management coursework, NAHB Chapter participation, industry engagement, work/volunteer experience, career plans, and financial need.

rows.name: Strategies for Success Scholarship
values: National Housing Endowment / NAHB Professional Women in Building

This scholarship encourages students to further their education in housing industry-related programs. Applicant must be pursuing study in a residential related program such as construction management, building, construction technology, civil engineering, architecture, design or any of the trade specialties. Must be registered as a full-time student with at least one full academic year of coursework remaining.
Housing Industry-Related Programs, Construction Management, Building, Construction Technology, Civil Engineering, Architecture, Design, Trade Specialties

rows.name: Building Hope Scholarship
values: National Housing Endowment / NAHB Professional Women in Building

This scholarship encourages students to further their education in housing industry-related programs. Applicants must be enrolled as full-time or part-time students at the start of the fall semester at a college, university or trade school with at least one course or trade related program remaining. Must be pursuing an education in a residential building related course of study or residential vocational/trade program. Awards cover tuition and school/program fees, paid directly to the institution.
Residential Building Related Course of Study, Residential Vocational/Trade Program

rows.name: Leadership Scholarship
values: National Housing Endowment / NAHB Professional Women in Building

Applicants must have an NAHB PWB membership in good standing. Preference may be given to PWB members who have served in PWB leadership roles at the local and/or national levels. Applicants must submit a complete application with letters of recommendation by the application deadline.

rows.name: NHE NAHB Remodelers Leadership Program
values: Financial support to help defray costs associated with member travel expenses

This program aims to provide exposure to NAHB leadership meetings to foster future leaders in the residential remodeling industry. Grant recipients receive financial support for travel expenses to NAHB’s Spring Leadership Meeting and access to networking events with leadership development opportunities. Open to current or past local leaders interested in national leadership.

rows.name: Associates Leadership Grant
values: Financial assistance to help defray the cost of attending NAHB’s board meetings

This grant develops active Associate leaders through mentoring, participation at national meetings, and education about NAHB’s programs and services. It provides financial assistance to Associate members to help defray the cost of attending NAHB’s board meetings, cultivating future leaders.

rows.name: Skin Grip Diabetes Scholarship
values: This scholarship supports high school seniors, undergraduate (2- or 4-year), and graduate students living with diabetes. It recognizes their resilience and determination in managing their condition while pursuing their education. The scholarship will be awarded to 24 individuals who live fearlessly with diabetes, requiring applicants to submit a short video.

rows.name: SEMA Memorial Scholarship Fund
values: The SEMA Memorial Scholarship Fund supports students pursuing careers in the automotive industry. Applicants must be incoming freshmen (18 years old by submission) or continuing students in college, university, or post-secondary career and technology schools in the United States. The scholarship aims to foster the next generation of automotive aftermarket industry leaders and innovators.

Automotive industry careers including accounting, engineering, race car driver/crew, administration information technology, sales/marketing, advertising, business, manufacturing, technician, design/graphics, photography/journalism, and transportation.

rows.name: Cards Against Humanity Science Ambassador Scholarship
values: Cards Against Humanity Science Ambassador Scholarship

This is an annual $20,000 tuition scholarship funded by Cards Against Humanity for women and non-binary students pursuing a degree in science, technology, engineering, or math. Applicants must be high school seniors or undergraduate college students and are required to submit a three-minute educational video explaining a STEM topic.

rows.name: Amtrak Academic Scholarship
values: The Amtrak Academic Scholarship supports undergraduate and graduate students pursuing degrees with an active interest in the railroad industry. It aims to encourage academic achievement within railroad programs. Applicants must meet a minimum GPA requirement and submit a resume and an essay related to rail transportation.

rows.name: Hilton Cares Scholarship Program
values: The Hilton Cares Scholarship Program is offered by the Hilton Global Foundation. This scholarship is likely intended for students pursuing education or careers within the hospitality industry.

rows.name: Anne Ford Scholarship
values: The Anne Ford Scholarship is for graduating high school seniors with documented learning disabilities who plan to enroll in a full-time bachelor's degree program. It supports their pursuit of a four-year post-secondary education and career advancement goals, with financial need being a factor in selection.

rows.name: Allegra Ford-Thomas Scholarship
values: The Allegra Ford Thomas Scholarship is a $5,000 scholarship awarded over two years ($2,500 each year) to graduating high school seniors. It supports students with documented learning disabilities (LD) who plan to enroll in a two-year community college, a vocational or technical training program, or a specialized program for students with disabilities. Financial need is a factor in the selection process.

rows.name: Anne Ford Scholarship
values: The Anne Ford Scholarship is for graduating high school seniors enrolling in a full-time bachelor's degree program. Applicants must have a documented learning disability (LD), and those with ADHD and LD are encouraged to apply. It provides $2,500 per year for four years.

rows.name: Allegra Ford Thomas Scholarship
values: The Allegra Ford Thomas Scholarship is for graduating high school seniors enrolling in a two-year community college, vocational/technical training, or a specialized program for students with disabilities. Applicants must have a documented learning disability (LD), and those with ADHD and LD are encouraged to apply. It provides $2,500 per year for two years.

rows.name: Everyday Champion Award
values: The Everyday Champion Award recognizes K-12 educators, paraprofessionals, and school-related service providers who excel in supporting students with learning disabilities. Recipients are awarded $5,000 for their positive impact on students' lives through personalized learning, mental health support, and inclusive practices.

rows.name: 2024-2025 ADHD Scholarship
values: This scholarship is for the 2024-2025 academic year and focuses on students with ADHD. Further details regarding eligibility and amount are available upon logging into the application portal.

rows.name: COVID-19 Impact Scholarship
values: This scholarship addresses the impact of COVID-19. Further details are not available on the specific page, which is currently a 404 error. Applicants may need to check the main portal for information.

rows.name: Wells Fargo Stacey Milbern Scholarship
values: The Wells Fargo Stacey Milbern Scholarship supports students with disabilities pursuing higher education or training in the US. Applicants must have a minimum 3.0 GPA, be a US citizen or legal resident, and demonstrate financial need. Awards range from $1,250 to $2,500 and are renewable for eligible full-time or half-time undergraduate study.

rows.name: Fred J. Epstein Youth Achievement Award
values: Fred J. Epstein Youth Achievement Award

This scholarship, the Fred J. Epstein Youth Achievement Award, is offered by Smart Kids with Learning Disabilities. It aims to recognize and celebrate the accomplishments of young individuals who have learning differences.

rows.name: Microsoft Disability Scholarship Program
values: The Seattle Foundation and the Disability at Microsoft Inclusion Network (administered by Scholarship America)

This scholarship assists current high school seniors with disabilities who plan to pursue higher education in college or vocational school. Applicants must be pursuing eligible majors in Engineering, Computer Science, Business, Law, or related fields, demonstrate a passion for technology and leadership, and require financial assistance.
Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Information Systems, Law, Business, Paralegal, Pre-Law, Finance, Business Administration, Marketing, Technology

rows.name: The Neurodiversity Scholarship
values: The Neurodiversity Scholarship is a national program for neurodivergent students (ages 16-26) with learning differences like Dyslexia, ADHD, Processing Disorders, or Autism. It provides financial aid for Associate, Bachelor, or Certificate programs at non-profit colleges/universities in the US, along with access to an online community and networking opportunities.

rows.name: Wells Fargo Stacey Milbern Scholarship
values: The Wells Fargo Stacey Milbern Scholarship is designed to help students with disabilities pursue education or training. Applicants must have an identified disability, a minimum 3.0 GPA, and be enrolled or planning to enroll in undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college or university. Financial need must be demonstrated.

rows.name: The Susanna and Lucy DeLaurentis Charitable Foundation Memorial Scholarships
values: The Susanna and Lucy DeLaurentis Charitable Foundation, 7616 Mountain Avenue, Elkins Park, PA 19027
The Susanna and Lucy DeLaurentis Charitable Foundation Memorial Scholarships

This scholarship is for college-bound high school seniors who demonstrate superior academic and extracurricular achievements while contending with a chronic disease or serious physical or mental health challenge. It honors the memory of Susanna and Lucy DeLaurentis, who faced significant health issues.
Chronic disease or serious physical or mental health challenge

rows.name: Pride Foundation Scholarship (Learning Differences)
values: This scholarship program supports LGBTQ+ students who are leaders in their communities and committed to advancing justice. It prioritizes students facing systemic barriers, family rejection, housing instability, poverty, and those demonstrating financial need. Applicants must be residents of Alaska, Idaho, Montana, Oregon, or Washington and pursuing post-secondary education.
Any, with specific funds for various majors/backgrounds, including learning differences

rows.name: All-American Pest Control STEAM Trailblazer Scholarship
values: All-American Pest Control STEAM Trailblazer Scholarship

The All-American Pest Control STEAM Trailblazer Scholarship empowers young women pursuing careers in Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics (STEAM). Applicants must be high school seniors or college/trade school students in the US with a minimum 3.0 GPA, demonstrating commitment to the sponsor's core values. The scholarship awards $1,000 to one exceptional individual.

rows.name: Hilleman/Morelli Scholarship
values: The Hilleman/Morelli Scholarship, now managed by Montana State University, supports high school and college students with dyslexia pursuing STEM degrees. It provides financial, academic, leadership, and mentoring support. Applicants are selected based on academic, leadership, and career potential, with financial impact being a consideration.

rows.name: Krystal and Franklin H. Noble Endowed Scholarship
values: MSU Billings, Krystal and Franklin H. Noble Endowed Scholarship
Krystal and Franklin H. Noble Endowed Scholarship

This scholarship is for Montana residents who are graduates of a public high school in the Flathead Valley area.
